forcedCloseReason.description:
Set when the protocol closed this leg on the user's behalf rather than
the user asking for it — today only `loan_gap_backstop`, the ILP loan
protection flattening a position whose mark reached the loan floor.

The chain can't tell us this: the operator signs every user action, so
a backstop close is shape-identical to a user's own market close and the
indexer (which reads liquidations off the VENUE instruction
discriminators) records a plain `decrease`. Had the venue's own loan
stop won that race, `action_type` would already be `liquidation` for the
identical event. So this rides alongside `action_type` rather than
overwriting it — the PnL and fee paths keyed on `"decrease" |
"liquidation"` keep their existing meaning, and only the label changes.

pairsImpactFee.description:
Skew-impact share of this action's fee, already included in
`jupiterFee`. Present only for pairs actions charged after the fee
mode shipped — `None` means no such fee was levied, NOT that it was
zero, so callers should omit the line rather than render 0.00.

ApiTouchPosition.description: One touch contract, open or finished.

askBps.description: Fill price as bps of payout (`premiumUsd / payoutUsd × 10000`).

expiryTs.description: Cohort expiry, unix seconds. Settlement is automatic at this time.

isTouch.description:
True = Touch (pays if spot ever reaches the barrier before expiry),
false = No-Touch (pays if it never does).

openTs.description: Cohort open, unix seconds — shared by every contract in the cohort.

payoutPaidUsd.description:
What the wallet actually received, µUSD — the payout on a win, the
buyback refund on a sell-back, 0 on a loss. Null while `open`.

payoutUsd.description: Payout if the contract wins, µUSD.

positionId.description:
Per-market contract id, from 0. Send `positionId + 1` as `triggerPrice`
to sell this contract back — see the "Imperial Touch" guide.

premiumUsd.description: Premium actually paid at the fill, µUSD — never the staged budget.

settleTxSig.description: Signature of the settle or buyback transaction. Null while `open`.

status.description:
`open` — live; `settled` — expired and paid out by the keeper;
`bought_back` — sold back to the pool before expiry.

won.description:
Whether the contract paid out. Null while `open`, and on a buyback
(which resolves the contract before the outcome is known).

ArmadaBalances.description:
Snapshot-only balance monitor. Thresholds share the treasury report's model;
transfers and pledged customer funds stay separate from owned capital.

customerFunds.description: Settled customer collateral plus pending request escrow, wherever held.

estimatedOwedToUsers.description:
Nonnegative claims per seat, including marked PnL, before funding/exit fees.
Older snapshots do not contain this estimate.

inFlightToHedge.description: Model-observed transfers, not confirmed destination balances.

ArmadaBookLevel.description: One aggregated level, in the venue's own `PRICE / SIZE / TOTAL` shape.

quoteSize.description: Sum of the original price times size, before display grouping.

total.description:
Base at this level and every better one. Sent rather than left to the
client to accumulate, so a truncated response cannot disagree with the
walk a quote is priced off.

ArmadaCapitalStatus.description:
The public status: ratios, an enum and a boolean. **No dollar figures.**

⚠ Nothing here may leak the size of Imperial's book — that is the whole
reason it is a separate type from [`ArmadaTreasuryResponse`] rather than a
projection of it, so a field added to the report cannot arrive here by
accident.

opensOpen.description:
Whether opens are being taken. `false` with no snapshot: no capital view
is `Limit::NoCapitalView`, which refuses opens.

tillRatio.description: The share of locked margin the till holds back.

utilisation.description:
Initial margin over total account value on the hedge venue — how much of
the account the hedge consumes. A ratio, so it says nothing about size.

ArmadaDecline.description:
Why a served quote was withheld. Every variant is an expected outcome, not
a fault: the caller spills the order to another venue.

markets.description:
Empty when nothing was requested in the window. A market with no rows is
a market with no traffic, not a market with zero slippage.

reserveCapBps.description: Conservative cap across configured depth-dependent closing reserves.

ArmadaMarginResponse.description:
One Armada seat's balance, and what of it pays out when.

⚠ Every money field is `Option`. A seat the api could not read reports
`null`, never `0` — an unknown balance rendered as zero is a recorded
product bug, and the client shows "—" for it.

arrivingEtaSecs.description:
How long the rest takes: the outbound rail's MEASURED settlement, not
the (deliberately pessimistic) window the till is sized over.

freeCollateralUsd.description:
Equity after current losses, funding, initial margin and the withdrawal
buffer, capped by settled free cash. Null when health is unavailable.

liquidationThresholdMinUsd.description: Authorized threshold range. Execution depth selects a value within it.

primeBound.description: Prime-bound seats currently support full closes only; collateral edits are unavailable.

withdrawableNowUsd.description:
`min(free collateral, vault balance − escrow)` — what the vault can
actually pay this instant.

withdrawableTotalUsd.description: The whole free balance, some of which may be arriving.

ArmadaMarket.description:
One market Armada will quote, with everything a market list renders.

⚠ Mirrors the venue's own parameters rather than restating ours. Imperial
must never advertise a cap looser than the venue carrying the risk, and the
only way that stays true across an upgradable contract is to read it back.

oneOf.description: Present only when a fresh on-chain lending policy is ready for new isolated market opens.

fundingRate1hPct.description:
The rate accruing over the CURRENT funding hour, as the venue publishes
it: a PERCENT, so `0.0025` renders as `0.0025%`. the hedge venue funds hourly.

⚠ Off the websocket, not off `orderBookDetails` — the catalog carries
the funding PARAMETERS (clamps, premium multiplier) but not the rate.
`None` for a market whose stats have aged out, which a client must
render as unknown rather than as zero: a market paying nothing and a
market we cannot read are different facts.

imperialFundingRate1hPct.description:
Armada's own live on-chain rate, hourly percent (positive: longs pay).
Absent when unread or stale; never substitute the hedge venue's rate.

oneOf.description: Imperial's own opening-ticket risk inputs, not the hedge venue's MMR.

listedAt.description:
Unix seconds. `None` when the venue omitted it.

⚠ Load-bearing, not decoration: a market younger than the VaR window has
no measurable tail, and a mark series from before it listed is not a
price history — it is noise that reads as enormous volatility.

marketId.description: The venue's market id. Stable, and what the book channels are keyed on.

maxLeverage.description: Lower of the hedge market's leverage and Imperial's on-chain ceiling.

mmr.description: Maintenance margin as a fraction of notional.

openInterest.description: Base units from `orderBookDetails`. Multiply by mark price for USD OI.

sizeDecimals.description:
Smallest base increment the venue accepts. A close below one lot cannot
be hedged, which is what stranded sub-lot dust on every full close until
the rounding was made leg-aware.

acceptRate.description:
Accepted over settled. ⚠ The denominator EXCLUDES pending, so a window
full of in-flight requests reads as the rate of what has actually
settled rather than being dragged toward zero by rows with no outcome
yet. `None` when nothing has settled — never 1.0.

adverseBps.description: The adverse edge: 9 in 10 fills landed better than this.

filledSizeUsd.description: What the venue filled, in USD.

hedgeVenue.description:
The venue that BACKED the fills, or that the refusals were aimed at.
`"any"` where the request named none — a different fact from naming the
venue that happens to be live, and kept as one.

market.description:
The asset key. Not a mint: most of what this venue exists to reach has
no Solana token.

medianBps.description:
Median of the signed fill-vs-expected series. **Positive means the fill
was BETTER for the user than the price the order stated.** `None` for a
window with no fills — never `0.0`, which is a real and different
answer.

pending.description: Still in flight, or settled by a transaction this service never saw.

rejects.description: Why the rejects were rejected. Empty when there were none.

ArmadaMarketStats.description:
The venue's published numbers for one market, alongside its book.

Carried on the same response as the book because they are read from the same
feed under the same freshness rule — splitting them into a second endpoint
would let a client render a mark from one moment against a book from
another, which is the exact pairing [`FeedState::quote_inputs`] exists to
prevent on the pricing side.

[`FeedState::quote_inputs`]: armada_client::FeedState::quote_inputs

fundingRate1hPct.description:
The rate accruing over the CURRENT funding hour, as the HEDGE VENUE
publishes it: a PERCENT, so `0.0025` renders as `0.0025%`. the hedge venue funds
hourly, so this is its `1HR FUNDING` with no rescaling.

⚠ **This is not what a Armada position is charged.** It is what the
venue carrying Imperial's hedge charges Imperial, published because it
is real, public and worth seeing beside the book it belongs to. What the
user pays is [`Self::imperial_funding_rate_1h_pct`], and a surface that
renders one under the other's label is telling the user something false.

imperialFundingRate1hPct.description:
**Imperial's own** funding rate on this market, hourly percent, signed so
that positive ⇒ longs pay shorts. Read off the `imperial_sunrise`
`FundingIndex` account, so it is what the program will actually settle.
`None` when no rate is in force on chain — no accumulator yet, or the
last publication is past `max_funding_staleness_secs`, in which case
nothing accrues.

⚠ Not derivable from [`Self::funding_rate_1h_pct`]. The publisher folds
in Imperial's own book skew and scales by the book's marked-to-entry
ratio (the program charges on entry notional; the venue bills Imperial on
marked), so this is not the venue's rate plus a spread.

markPrice.description:
The venue's own mark — what it margins and liquidates against, and the
price a Armada quote is anchored to.

nextFundingAtMs.description:
Unix ms at which the current funding hour settles. `None` unless the
venue's timestamp is genuinely ahead of now and inside
[`MAX_FUNDING_LOOKAHEAD_MS`] — a past timestamp is the LAST funding, and
labelling it "next" is worse than showing nothing.

⚠ Belongs to [`Self::funding_rate_1h_pct`] alone. Imperial's own accrual
is CONTINUOUS — `rate × dt` for whatever `dt` a position existed, with no
concept of an hour — so there is no next-funding instant to count down
to, which is exactly why the open-after/close-before game does not work
here.

acceptRate.description: `None` before the first request, rather than a misleading 1.0.

ArmadaOrderbook.description: The hedge venue's live book for one market, as the trading panel renders it.

bids.description: Best price first: bids descending, asks ascending.

bookAgeMs.description:
⚠ Milliseconds since the book last **changed**, not since it was
confirmed. A quiet market's book ages without the venue going anywhere,
so a client must not read this as liveness — [`Self::venue_reachable`]
is that signal.

hedgeVenue.description: Whose book this is, in the same literal `/armada/status` reports.

maxAgeMs.description:
The carry bound this book was served under, so a client can render its
own staleness without hard-coding a number the server owns.

venueReachable.description:
Whether ANY event has arrived from the venue recently, across every
channel. This is what says the venue is still there.

ArmadaPrimeCapability.description: A loan capability supplied only after on-chain policy and launch readiness checks.

allInBps.description: What the user pays over the mark, all in.

chargedHedgeCostBps.description:
What the user is actually charged for the hedge: `max(hedge_cost, 0)`
after the risk gate's widen multiplier.

hedgeBaseSize.description:
Base units the hedge will be sent in. The unit the venue's lot step
rounds, and therefore the unit the unhedged residual lives in.

hedgeCostBps.description:
Marginal cost of hedging THIS order at THIS size, as measured: the walk's
signed slippage against the mark plus the venue's flat taker fee.

SIGNED, and can be negative when the mark happens to sit on the far side
of the touch. Recorded as measured because it is the input to grading;
the quote itself floors it at zero (see `charged_hedge_cost_bps`) rather
than paying a user for a book/mark relationship the hedge may not
capture a second later.

hedgeWorstPrice.description: The limit an IOC hedge would need to carry to fill this size.

mark.description:
The venue mark the quote was struck against. Persisted so markout can be
graded against it after the fill.

quotePrice.description: `mark ± all_in`, on the side the user trades.

ArmadaRejectCount.description: One reject reason's share of a window.

reasonName.description:
The reason's stable wire name, from the program. `null` for a byte this
deployment does not classify — which means the chain and this binary
disagree, and inventing a label would hide that.

ArmadaSettledMetrics.description:
The venue-wide settlement record, summed across every market in the window.

⚠⚠ This is NOT the same number as [`crate::sunrise::metrics`]'s accept rate
and the two must never be presented as one. The in-process counter measures
the GATE: how many orders the risk check admitted, where a refusal never
reached the chain and left no row anywhere. This measures what happened to
the requests that DID reach the chain. A gate refusal is absent from this
denominator entirely, and a request rejected on chain is absent from that
one. Both are real; conflating them would produce a rate describing neither.

acceptRate.description: `None` when nothing has settled in the window — never 1.0.

rejectsByReason.description:
Pooled across markets, because the claim being checked — that rejects
are uncorrelated with price direction — is a claim about the venue.

markets.description:
Per-`(hedge_venue, market)`, because none of the state behind a phase
nets across venues.

metrics.description:
⚠ THE GATE's accept rate, and markout. In-process, so it resets on every
deploy — which is a real limit on it as a "published commitment", and
the reason [`Self::settled`] exists beside it. What it measures cannot
come from the chain: a gate refusal never becomes a request, so it
leaves no row anywhere. Markout is the same — it samples the venue's mid
one and two seconds after a quote, and nothing on chain records a later
mid — so it stays here and is honestly per-process.

oneOf.description:
⚠ THE CHAIN's accept rate, over a trailing window of `sunrise_requests`.
Survives a restart, and answers a DIFFERENT question from `metrics`: of
the requests that actually reached the chain, how many filled. A gate
refusal is absent from this denominator; an on-chain reject is absent
from that one. `None` when the ledger is unreadable — this endpoint's
job is to say whether the venue is fit to serve, and that must not go
dark because Postgres hiccuped.

ArmadaTreasuryResponse.description:
The whole read. Every section is `None` before the treasury loop has ever
written a snapshot — a well-formed body, never a 500.

capacity.description:
Empty when the api has no account view of the hedge venue. Capacity is
computed from the api's OWN feed, not from the snapshot, because it is
the answer to "may I open now", and the snapshot is minutes old.

oneOf.description:
The api's own the hedge venue floor against the bot's. `None` when the api could
not recompute one — no account view, or no snapshot to compare with.

amount.description: Deposit amount in USDC native units (6-decimal — `1_000_000` = $1).

deferOperatorSignature.description:
Return the transaction with the operator's signature slot still empty,
to be handed back to `/deposit/cosign-tx` once the wallet has signed
it. Wallets can't simulate a transaction that already carries a
signature from another account, so they warn the user that it may be
unsafe; signing second avoids that. Defaults to false, which returns
the partially-signed transaction described below.

mode.description:
`"deposit"` to credit USDC directly from the wallet's USDC ATA into the
profile's USDC ATA, or `"withdraw"` to pull USDC out of the profile back
to the wallet's USDC ATA. Funding from native SOL is not supported —
wrap to WSOL on the client first.

profileIndex.description: Sub-account index (0..5) the deposit lands in.

wallet.description:
Owner wallet base58 pubkey. The returned tx is partially signed by the
order-bot operator (sponsoring rent + ATA creation) and must be signed
by this wallet before submission.

transaction.description:
Base64-encoded `VersionedTransaction`. Decode, sign with the wallet's
keypair, and submit via your usual RPC.

transactionSignature.description: NULL while the payout is pending; only signed payouts reduce claimable.

accruedUsdcBase.description: Lifetime builder fees accrued across both order legs (6-dp USDC).

paidUsdcBase.description: Lifetime settled payouts (rows with a transaction signature).

payouts.description: Latest 50 payouts, newest first (includes pending unsigned rows).

CloseSlippageBand.description:
One (market, venue, leg) band. All figures are signed basis points of the
trigger price, normalized so **negative means the fill was worse for the
user** — identical convention on long and short.

adverseBps.description:
The adverse edge — the 10th percentile of the signed series, i.e. 9 in
10 fills landed better than this. Percentile rather than a moment
because fill slippage has a long adverse tail (a single 4.5% gap fill
in the sample would drag a mean into uselessness).

formulaVersion.description:
Which definition of "quoted" the band is measured against: 1 is the
browser's TP/SL preview, 2 a server-struck Armada quote. Part of the
band's identity, not a label — averaging two versions together produces
a number that describes neither. Bands arrive ascending by it, so a
consumer keyed on (market, venue, leg) alone lands on the newest.

leg.description:
`"tp"`, `"sl"`, or `"entry"`. Kept separate because they are not
interchangeable: stops fill adversely and take profits roughly don't, so
pooling them would understate the stop band and invent one for take
profits.

medianBps.description: Typical fill. The centre of the quoted range.

bands.description:
Only markets that cleared `min_samples`. A market absent from this list
has no usable history — the client must show its point estimate rather
than inventing a band.

minSamples.description: The floor actually applied, after clamping.

CostBreakdown.description:
Expected ROUND-TRIP cost model over the requested `holdHours` window.
Only `openFee`/`openSlip` are paid at open time; every other term is a
LIFECYCLE EXPECTATION — an estimate of what the position will cost over its
life, never reserved or deducted upfront. Do NOT size deposits from this
(integrators that did over-funded ~15x); use `requiredDeposit`, which is
the explicit upfront number.

borrow.description:
Lifecycle estimate: borrow/funding cost over the FULL `holdHours`
window, accrued hourly while the position is open. Not upfront.

closeFee.description:
Lifecycle estimate: close fee weighted by `(1 − pLiq)` — expected
amount paid on voluntary close. Not an upfront cost.

closeSlip.description: Lifecycle estimate: close slippage weighted by `(1 − pLiq)`.

expectedLiqCost.description:
Lifecycle estimate: `pLiq × LossGivenLiq(venue)` — a probabilistic
liquidation-loss reserve, NOT a fee and NOT a funding requirement.

loanCost.description:
Lifecycle estimate: Imperial Lending Pool borrow cost over the hold
period. Present only when a loan split applies to this venue (see
`fold_loan_into_cost`).

openFee.description: UPFRONT: the venue's open fee, deducted from collateral at open.

total.description:
Expected round-trip cost (sum of the above). A comparison metric
between venues — never what must sit in the wallet/profile.

totalIn.description: Total into profiles (micro-USD magnitude), USD-valued rows only.

totalOut.description: Total out of profiles (micro-USD magnitude), USD-valued rows only.

amount.description: Signed raw token units (native decimals); positive = into the profile.

amountUsd.description: Signed micro-USD. Omitted for mints with no USD valuation.

counterparty.description:
Source owner for deposits, destination wallet for withdrawals, the
other profile PDA for transfers.

counterpartyProfileIndex.description: The other profile's index for transfer legs.

DepositHistoryAnnotation.description:
Operator-added context for a verified transfer. Never sourced from an
on-chain memo, and never changes the transfer's classification or amounts.

fetchedAt.description:
Wall-clock time the most recent message landed, in milliseconds since
the unix epoch. Use this to gate routing on freshness (drop Phoenix
when `now − fetched_at > STALE_THRESHOLD_MS`).

sigmaBpsPerSqrtSec.description:
Short-horizon realized volatility of this book's mid, in basis points
per √second — multiply by √(seconds) for the expected move over a
horizon. `None` until enough mid ticks have accumulated to mean
anything; callers must not substitute zero for "unknown".

loanInterest.description:
ILP loan interest paid to the lending pool (distinct from the venue
borrow/funding `interest` line). None = no loan.

pairsImpactFee.description:
Skew-impact share of `jupiter_fee`, summed over this position's
actions. A COMPONENT of that line, not an addition. Absent when no
action carried one — which is not the same as zero, so the display
omits the row rather than showing 0.00. Derived from the actions
rather than a lifecycle counter: an accumulating column would be a
non-idempotent write racing three indexer workers.

FloorDriftReport.description:
The api's the hedge venue floor against the order bot's, with the tolerance it was
judged at.

apiFloor.description: Recomputed here, from the api's own venue feed.

botFloor.description: As the treasury loop stored it.

FundingModel.description:
How collateral reaches the venue when opening a position. Branch on this
BEFORE opening:
- `self_funding`: the open transaction pulls collateral straight from your
  wallet's USDC ATA, atomically. Do NOT pre-deposit — the deposit would
  land in escrow, go unused (the open never reads it), and only get swept
  back to your wallet minutes later, looking like a double-charge. Jupiter,
  Phoenix, and GMTrade are self-funding.
- `prefund_v2`: the open draws from your profile's staged deposit ledger,
  so collateral must be in place before opening. The ER/basket venues —
  Imperial Pairs — and Armada use this.

GmTradeFundingRatesResponse.description:
Per-symbol funding/borrow/net rates for the bot use case. All fields are
percentages (0.04 = 0.04%) at hourly cadence, sourced from the GMTrade WS
`indexTokens` feed and refreshed every 5 minutes. Sign convention follows
GMTrade's: a positive `longFundingRatePerHourPercent` means longs pay shorts.

GmTradeLiquidityResponse.description:
Per-symbol pool headroom (USD) for the preferred (open, USDC-collateral
first) market variant. `null` on either side means the on-chain liquidity
poller hasn't seen that symbol yet, or the data couldn't be parsed.

HedgeCapital.description:
The the hedge venue side of the capital state, in the lines the plan names.

Six lines rather than one float, because the decision this feeds — add seed
money, or don't — is made from measured numbers and a single "we're fine"
scalar cannot be argued with.

distance.description: TAV above the opens-stop line. Negative means opens are stopped.

exitRequirement.description: Capital for selective exits; absent on snapshots from the old model.

floor.description: Below this a top-up hop is due.

funding.description: Signed as the snapshot stores it: negative is funding we pay.

held.description: Imperial's float plus what has been pledged.

tav.description: Total account value: what is held, marked.

ImperialLines.description:
The six telemetry lines the plan kept after chapter 4 was removed.

⚠⚠ **Every one of these is an OBSERVATION, not a requirement.** Nothing here
is a floor, a gate, or a number any code sizes against; they are the
decomposition an operator reads to decide whether the $30k seed
([`sunrise_capital::config::DEFAULT_FLOAT_CAP_USD`]) needs growing, and the
seed is grown from what the book shows rather than declared up front.

A line the api genuinely cannot compute is `None`, never zero — see each
field for why.

badDebtWorst.description:
The worst loss users could leave past the margin they posted.

⚠ **Always `None` here**, and not for want of a book.
[`sunrise_capital::stress`] makes this identically ZERO for every book
and every move while `Shock::fill_move` is `None` — the liquidator
closes a losing seat AT its line, so the loss never exceeds the margin,
and the arithmetic reduces to `-notional × maintenance_margin`, clamped
at zero. A non-zero figure exists only once a SLOWER liquidator is
priced, and how much slower is a policy input the api has no reading of.
Publishing the structural zero as though it were a measurement would say
"no bad debt is possible" when what is true is "none is modelled".

closeoutCost.description:
What taking the whole hedge off costs in the venue's own fees:
`Σ |net| × liquidation_fee_fraction`, per market.

⚠ Fees only. It does not walk the book, so it excludes the fill
slippage a real unwind pays — the model prices that separately as
`unwind_slippage`, which is a scenario parameter rather than something
the api measures. `None` when the venue account view is unreadable.

floorGapHedge.description:
Floor that Imperial's float plus the whole pledgeable pool cannot reach
— `Floors::capital_short_usd`, recovered from the row. This is the line
that says "add capital on the hedge venue".

hopBudget.description:
The dollars the current state's top-up hop would have to move:
`max(0, floor − tav)`. Zero is the healthy answer and is a measurement,
not an absence.

nakedLeg.description:
User exposure Imperial carries with no hedge behind it:
`Σ |user net − hedge net|` across every market either side names.

The user book comes from the snapshot's `per_market.book`, the hedge
from the api's own live venue feed. ⚠ The two are therefore read at
DIFFERENT instants, so anything that traded since the snapshot shows up
here — this line has a noise floor, and a small non-zero reading on a
busy book is lag rather than an unhedged position. `None` when either
side is unreadable.

seedSolana.description:
Vault shortfall against the Solana floor: `max(0, solana_floor −
balance)`. The line that says "add capital on Solana".

threshold.description: RSI threshold as a plain decimal string (e.g. "30").

timeframe.description: Numeric timeframe code as a string (FE maps to labels).

accruedFundingFrom.description:
Unix seconds when the `accrued_funding_usd` window opened: the last
action that booked interest into the ledger, else position open. NOT
`last_action_at` — Phoenix increases settle funding without booking
anything, so an add-only position's window reaches back to open even
though it was touched since (jax's SOL short: opened Jun 26, last
increase Jul 3 — labeling the accrual "since Jul 3" made Jun 26–Jul 3
look unrecorded, 2026-07-17).

accruedFundingUsd.description:
Funding accrued on this open position that Funding History has not
booked yet — i.e. exactly what the next reduce/close will write as a
`funding_events` row. Positive = the trader pays, matching
`tx2_interest_charged`. This is NOT `borrow_fee_owed`: on Phoenix it
also covers funding already cash-settled into collateral at an
increase, which is not owed at close but is likewise missing from the
ledger. Consumers showing "accrued funding" want this; consumers
showing due-on-close want `borrow_fee_owed`.

breakevenPriceUsd.description:
Phoenix only: price the open residue must reach to recover residual
fees/funding (kernel breakeven). None for non-Phoenix and closed positions.

liqBandPriceUsd.description:
Worst acceptable liquidation fill (trigger ± 3× premium) — the
venue-enforced execution-band limit of the backstop stop: a cap on a
short's buy-back, a FLOOR on a long's sell. Phoenix loan rows only.

liqTriggerPriceUsd.description:
The loan-protection threshold (breakeven ∓ premium) — where the
liquidation fill should AVERAGE, and where the venue backstop stop
rests. Phoenix loan rows only (Flash/Jupiter loan stops fill at
oracle price — no orderbook band semantics). On closed rows: the
armed trigger persisted at settle.

loanOriginationNotionalUsd.description:
The obligation's ORIGINATION notional (frozen at open / top-up; NOT
mark-adjusted), 6-dec USD string. This is the notional the on-chain
`min_loan_bps` floor measures, so loan-sizing consumers (the FE add
quote) must floor against it — the live mark-adjusted notional drifts
below it on a dip and under-sizes the add-loan (Custom 77 forever,
VVV order DaRZTRA…, 2026-07-07). Open loan rows only.

loanRateBps.description: Our live bucket rate on the loan, bps APR.

netCashPnlUsd.description:
Realized net cash PnL for a closed/liquidated position: total USDC the
user got back across close legs minus total USDC they put in across
opening legs. `pnl_usd` is gross price PnL with costs booked in the
separate fee columns; this cash figure already absorbs every cost the
user actually paid — open and close fees, interest and funding, the
swap-to-USDC fee and slippage on long closes, and Flash's borrow fee
(which no fee column records). None while the position is open, and when
a close leg has no recorded received amount or there is no deposit
basis, so the frontend falls back to `pnl_usd`. Also None for Flash V2,
whose `tx3_user_received` is derived synthetically (collateral + profit −
loss) and so would collapse to gross price PnL rather than real net cash.

openingSlot.description:
Indexed opening evidence: a cached account deletion from an older slot
cannot disprove a later reopening of the same Armada seat.

ourLiquidationPriceUsd.description:
Imperial's (tighter) liquidation price — REPLACES the venue liq price
in every display when present (safety requirement, D7). For OPEN
Phoenix loan rows this is the book-aware FIRE level: the mark at
which the bot's liquidator closes the whole position so the fill
averages ≈ `liq_trigger_price_usd`. For closed/liquidated rows it is
the armed trigger frozen at settle.

oneOf.description:
Present only on a position a perp pack handed over.

★★★ EVERY OTHER FIELD ON THIS RESPONSE STAYS TRUE. The story lives here
and nowhere else, so a surface that has not opted in shows the real open
— see the note on `apply_pack_backdate` for the compute sites that made
overwriting in place the wrong call.

partialLiquidationPriceUsd.description:
Phoenix only: maintenance-breach (partial/first-liquidation) price from
the effective-collateral margin kernel. None for non-Phoenix and closed
positions. Distinct from `liquidation_price`, which is left unchanged.

seatCollateralUsd.description:
Phoenix only: the LIVE gross seat collateral on the trader account = the
user's own collateral PLUS the loan already deposited on the seat, read
from the same on-chain trader account this endpoint already decodes. This
is the basis Phoenix's margin check (and the api add-headroom gate) uses,
versus `collateral_usd` which is the user's own collateral net of the
loan. The frontend needs it to size a loaned add against the same basis
the chain enforces. Present only on loan-backed Phoenix positions.

sunriseMarginSeat.description: Armada margin seat: null is cross; an asset key identifies isolation.

phoenixCrossSeats.description:
Account-level state of each Phoenix cross-margin seat backing a position in
`data_list`, one entry per profile. Empty for every wallet with no unified
(cross) margin profile.

On a cross seat these are the ONLY numbers that describe risk: collateral,
margin and liquidation are properties of the seat, not of any one leg, so the
rows themselves carry no `liquidationPrice`. See "Cross margin (unified
margin)" in the API overview.

In the same response rather than a separate endpoint: it removes a round trip
and, more importantly, the consistency window — a user cannot see positions
from one instant next to the margin figures from another, which for a
liquidation-relevant number is the difference between reassuring and wrong.
`GET /api/v1/phoenix/margin-account` serves the same object on its own, for
when the profile holds no positions yet.

Absent when Phoenix's trader-state read failed. Treat that as unknown, never
as `0`.

oneOf.description:
Present only when the new mode constrains routing — under `"unified"`
this is Phoenix. Apply it client-side; the api and order bot both reject
opens that violate it, but only after the round trip.

MarketCapacity.description: How much more net exposure one market can take.

longUsd.description: Dollars of additional NET LONG exposure before the opens-stop line.

shortUsd.description:
The same net short. Smaller than the long side by construction: a short
hedge's notional grows as the move goes against it.

meanBps.description:
`None` until a sample exists. Never report zero for "unmeasured" — the
measured value IS ~zero, so the two would be indistinguishable.

profiles.description: One entry per Imperial subaccount (profile_index 0..5), in order.

cascadeChildren.description:
Whether cancelling an entry order also cancels the pending TP/SL orders
linked to it (their `parentOrderPda` is this order). Defaults to `true`:
close orders are market/side-scoped on-chain, so ones that outlive their
entry order execute against whatever position exists on that market/side
next. Pass `false` only when the children should survive — e.g. the
"execute limit at market now" flow, where the cancel is immediately
followed by an equivalent market open the children are meant to protect.

orderPda.description: Base58 PDA of the order to cancel.

profileIndex.description: Sub-account index (0..5) the order belongs to.

wallet.description: Base58 wallet pubkey. Must match the JWT's wallet claim.

action.description:
0 = add collateral, 1 = remove collateral.

Removing from a cross seat is capped at
`effectiveCollateralForWithdrawalsUsd - initialMarginForWithdrawalsUsd`
from `GET /api/v1/phoenix/margin-account` — a stricter basis than free
margin.

collateralAmount.description: Amount of collateral to add or remove, in the collateral mint's native units.

marketMint.description:
Base58 SPL mint of the market whose position is being adjusted.

On a Phoenix cross-margin seat there is one balance behind every market,
so this (with `side`) only has to name a market the seat currently holds —
the funds land in the account either way.

price.description:
Client-observed market price. Same per-underwriter scale as `marketPrice` on
`/mobile/orders`: Jupiter/Phoenix micro-USD (1e6), Flash Trade target-exponent
(`price × 10^(-priceExponent)` from `GET /api/v1/flash/markets`), GMTrade 1e9.

requestedHedgeVenue.description:
Optional Armada execution constraint: 0 = automatic, 1 = current hedge route.
A selected route binds; reserved values are rejected. Use 0 for other underwriters.

sunriseMarginMode.description:
Armada position's actual margin seat: "cross" or "isolated". Omitted
by older clients, which resolve the seat from the existing position.

underwriter.description:
0 = Jupiter, 1 = Flash Trade, 2 = Phoenix, 3 = GMTrade, 4 = Flash Trade V2,
5 = Imperial Pairs, 6 = Imperial Touch, 7 = Imperial Armada.
Wire format mirrors `passthrough_client::Underwriter`.

Byte 7 does NOT identify a venue on its own — see
`requestedHedgeVenue`.

wallet.description: Base58 wallet pubkey. Must match the JWT's wallet claim.

delegate.description:
When set, this is a delegate-mode connect: `signature` is by this delegate
pubkey, which must match the on-chain `UserAccount.signer_delegate`.

message.description:
Plain message that was signed. Wallet mode: `imperial:mobile-connect:{wallet}:{nonce}`.
Delegate mode: `imperial:delegate-connect:{wallet}:{delegate}:{nonce}`.
`{nonce}` must be a current Unix timestamp (seconds or millis, e.g. `Date.now()`), not a
random value: it is rejected if >5 min old or >60s in the future, and is single-use.

signature.description:
Base58-encoded signature over `message`. Wallet mode: by `wallet`. Delegate
mode: by the registered `delegate` key.

code.description: One-time code to exchange for a JWT via `/mobile/exchange` within 5 minutes.

closeOrders.description:
Close-side legs (TP, SL, ratchet, DCA-close, ...) attached to the entry.
Each must have `action == 1` and match the entry's
`(wallet, marketMint, side, underwriter, profileIndex)` tuple.
One result per close leg, in input order. Empty if the entry failed.

entry.description: Result of the entry submission. `success = false` skips the close legs.

builderCode.description:
Optional builder code (case-insensitive; normalized to uppercase). The
code's fixed per-code bps rate is charged on top of the standard fee,
on both the open and close legs, on the same base as the flat
collateral fee. Unknown or deactivated codes are rejected with `400`.

closeBps.description:
For decrease orders (`action = 1`) only: fraction of the LIVE position
to close, in basis points (`10000` = full close, `2500` = a quarter).
Strongly recommended over `sizeUsd` for closes — it is evaluated
against the on-chain position size at execution, so it is immune to
the price drift that can turn a `sizeUsd`-denominated full close into
a dust-leaving partial (which Flash rejects with `MinCollateral`).
When set, `sizeUsd` is ignored for close sizing. A full close may
equivalently send `sizeUsd = 0` with this field omitted. Not yet
supported on DCA close order types (12/13/14), which still size each
leg from `sizeUsd`. Rejected with `400` on increase orders.

collateralAmount.description:
Collateral amount in the collateral mint's native units.

On a profile set to unified (cross) margin this is a top-up **deposit into
the Phoenix seat**, not the position's margin — the seat as a whole margins
every leg, so `0` is legal once the seat has free collateral. See "Cross
margin (unified margin)" in the API overview for the admission rule.

extraData.description:
Per-order-type parameters (e.g. `{ "worstPrice": ..., "ratchetSize": ... }`
for ratchet orders; `{ "dcaNumLegs": ..., "dcaIntervalSeconds": ... }` for DCA).
Armada orders may specify `sunriseSeat`: 0 = cross, 1 = isolated.
New increases otherwise use the profile preference; closes should carry
the target position's seat, which survives profile-mode changes.

fundingStatus.description:
Funding mode: 0 = funded at creation (collateral debited from the profile immediately),
1 = pending (the order is created without collateral and the order-bot funder tops it up
asynchronously). Most integrators want 0.

marketMint.description:
Base58 SPL mint of the market (e.g. SOL mint for SOL-PERP). Either this
or `symbol` must be set; if both are provided, `marketMint` wins.
Use `symbol` instead unless you already have a venue-specific mint and
want to skip the server-side lookup.

marketPrice.description:
Client-observed market price at the moment the order was placed.
Forwarded to the on-chain market-order instruction so the program can enforce slippage
against an agreed-upon reference price. Ignored for resting orders.

**Scale is per-underwriter** (unlike `triggerPrice`, which is always 1e9):
- Jupiter (0) and Phoenix (2): micro-USD, `price × 1e6`. SOL at $64.94 → `64940000`.
- Flash Trade (1): target-exponent encoding, `price × 10^(-priceExponent)`, where
  `priceExponent` is per-market (typically `-8`) from `GET /api/v1/flash/markets`.
  SOL at $64.94 with exponent `-8` → `6494000000`.
- GMTrade (3): oracle scale, `price × 1e9` → `64940000000`. (1e6 truncates
  sub-$0.001 assets like BONK to a zero slippage band.)
- Flash Trade V2 (4): ignored — V2 market orders execute on the MagicBlock ER
  without a client reference price. Send `0`.
- Imperial Pairs (5): micro-USD, as Jupiter and Phoenix.
- Imperial Touch (6): ignored — a touch buy pays a premium, not a slippage-bounded
  fill. Send `0`.
- Imperial Armada (7): micro-USD. ⚠ It becomes the request's `expected_price` on
  `imperial_sunrise` (rescaled to the program's 1e9), which is the reference BOTH
  on-chain price bands measure against — including the one protecting Imperial. A
  value far from the market is refused rather than filled.

parentOrderPda.description:
Optional Order PDA of the parent limit order this close order is
attached to. Set this when adding a TP/SL/Trailing to a still-resting
limit so the UI groups it under that limit (instead of relying on the
`(market, side, profile)` heuristic, which mis-groups close orders
across unrelated parents on the same key). NULL for standalone close
orders (i.e. attached to an open position) and for entry orders.

phoenixNative.description:
Opt into Phoenix's native CLOB for this order instead of the
keeper-managed IOC fallback. Only meaningful when `underwriter = 2`
(Phoenix) AND `orderType` is `Limit` (1) with `action = Increase` (0),
or `PrivateTpSl` (5). Ignored for any other shape.

Default behavior (unset / `false`): the API rewrites Phoenix Limit /
PrivateTpSl to StopLimit so the order routes through the keeper path.
That dodges a class of indexer + orderbook-watcher bugs that have
stranded user collateral in the past (cancel-cleanup races, slot
classification edges).

Set `true` only if you understand those risks and need genuine resting
CLOB orders — e.g. maker-fee arbitrage bots. Orders placed with
`phoenixNative = true` will not be rewritten and will rest natively on
the Phoenix orderbook.

priority.description:
Funding-queue ranking for resting orders. Lower value = higher priority (0 is highest).
Used by the order-bot funder to decide which `funding_status=1` orders to top up first
when the profile has constrained balance. Has no effect on Solana priority fees.

profileIndex.description:
Sub-account index (0..5). Profiles don't share balances or positions.
A profile is isolated-margin by default; one switched to unified margin
opens new positions on Phoenix's cross seat instead, and rejects opens on
every other venue. `GET /passthrough/users/{wallet}/profiles` reports the
mode.

quote.description:
What the client's close preview quoted for this order, captured so the
realized fill can later be measured against it. Purely diagnostic.

Deliberately opaque: a TYPED `Option<OrderQuotePayload>` here does NOT
isolate a bad quote — serde fails the whole request body, so the order
is rejected in the extractor before the handler ever runs, with no log
line and no `order_placement_events` row. That is exactly what happened
on 2026-08-09: `lifecycleId` carries `unifiedPositionRowId`
(`<pda>:<asset>:<side>`) for a Phoenix cross-seat row, which is not a
UUID, so every quoted TP/SL 400'd and users saw "Failed to create
order". Parsed AFTER the order lands, so a malformed quote costs the
diagnostic and nothing else.

quoteId.description:
Id of a quote the api served on `/armada/quote`.

Armada only. This is what makes the quote server-authoritative: the
client sends the id, not the numbers, and the api prices the order from
its own record of what it served. A quote binds to exactly one order and
expires — an unknown or stale id is ignored, not fatal, so an order is
never lost to a quote that aged out.

requestedHedgeVenue.description:
Optional Armada execution constraint: 0 = automatic, 1 = current hedge route.
A selected route binds; reserved values are rejected. Use 0 for other underwriters.

sizeUsd.description: Position size in USD, 6-decimal fixed point (1_000_000 = $1).

symbol.description:
Canonical Imperial symbol (e.g. `"SOL"`, `"XAU"`). Resolved server-side
to the right `marketMint` for the requested `underwriter` — this is the
recommended addressing path: the same symbol you read from
`/funding-rates` works directly here, including Phoenix synthetics
(XAU, SPY, EUR, GBP, …) that have no SPL mint of their own.

triggerCondition.description: 0 = Above, 1 = Below. Direction of trigger condition relative to price.

triggerPrice.description: Trigger price in oracle scale (1e9). Required for non-market orders.

underwriter.description:
0 = Jupiter, 1 = Flash Trade, 2 = Phoenix, 3 = GMTrade, 4 = Flash Trade V2,
5 = Imperial Pairs, 6 = Imperial Touch, 7 = Imperial Armada.
Wire format mirrors `passthrough_client::Underwriter`.

Byte 7 does NOT identify a venue on its own — see
`requestedHedgeVenue`.

wallet.description: Base58 wallet pubkey. Must match the JWT's wallet claim.

expiresAt.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the JWT expires.

jwt.description: JWT. Pass as `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on trading endpoints.

adjustedSizeUsd.description:
Set when the Phoenix add-headroom gate silently reduced the order's
`size_usd` so it would actually open (auto-clamp / "sluff down to
leverage"). Present only when a clamp happened; carries the final
6-decimal-USD size the order was submitted with. The FE surfaces this as
an informational "opened at a reduced size" note — it is not an error.

cancelledChildOrderPdas.description:
Cancel-only: PDAs of pending TP/SL orders linked to the cancelled order
(via `parentOrderPda`) that were cancelled along with it. On-chain
orders carry no parent binding — a close order that outlives its entry
order stays armed on the (profile, market, side) triple and executes
against whatever position exists there next, so the cancel cascades.

error.description: Humanized error message when `success` is false.

errorCode.description:
Machine-matchable error code for programmatic branching. Named codes
cover the stable rejection classes: `PostOnlyWouldCross`,
`LoanMarketNotWhitelisted`, `LoanVenueUnsupported`,
`SwapRouteUnavailable`, `MarketClosed`, `TradingPaused`,
`SlippageExceeded`, `PositionAlreadyClosed`, `ProfileHasOpenPositions`,
`CancelViaAppOnly`, `LoanSizeAddBreaksFloor`, `InsufficientBalance`,
`LeverageTooHigh`, `LeverageTooLow`, `MinCollateral`,
`ReduceBelowMinCollateral`, `InsufficientVenueBalance`,
`InsufficientMargin`. Any other on-chain rejection surfaces its raw
program error as `Custom<N>` (e.g. `Custom6024`). `None` on success and
on failures with no recognizable program code (read `error` for the
human-facing message).

oneOf.description:
Structured user-safe reason, outcome, and recovery guidance. Additive;
`error` and `errorCode` remain for existing integrations.

makerOnly.description:
Maker-only proof metadata (IMP-355). `makerOnly` is `true` when this
order is a Phoenix-native limit / TP — those always rest as
`OrderPacketKind::PostOnly` with slide disabled, so they can only ever
add liquidity. It is `false` for every other shape (keeper-rewritten
Phoenix limits, market orders, and all other underwriters), which take
or may take liquidity. There is no request field — maker-only is implied
by the order shape (see `imperial_venues::is_native_dispatch`).

orderPda.description:
Base58 Order PDA for **resting orders only** (limit, stop-limit, ratchet,
DCA, Phoenix native, etc.) — `None` for market orders, which open a
position rather than rest. Use this for downstream `/mobile/orders/cancel`
or `/mobile/orders/update` calls without polling the indexer to discover
the PDA. Deterministic — derived from the profile PDA + the
`user_account.order_counter` snapshot at placement.

postOnlyRejected.description:
`true` when a maker-only order was refused specifically because it would
have crossed the spread (taker fill) — the maker-only contract was
enforced by rejecting it. Always paired with `wouldCross = true` and
`errorCode = "PostOnlyWouldCross"`. No Order PDA, position, or trade is
created in this case.

signature.description: Solana transaction signature, if one was produced.

success.description: True if the order bot accepted the request.

wouldCross.description:
`true` when the requested limit price would immediately cross resting
liquidity and fill as taker. For a maker-only order this is the reason it
was rejected; it is the proof that the order was not silently downgraded
to a taker fill.

seasonName.description:
Name of the active points season, or `null` when no season is live
(in which case both points figures are `0`).

seasonPoints.description:
Whole-point figure as displayed on the Imperial homepage
(`seasonPointsMicros / 1_000_000`, floored).

seasonPointsMicros.description: Imperial points earned this season, in micro-points (6 decimals).

MobilePreflightResponse.description:
Verdict on an order the caller has NOT placed. `ok: false` is a 200 with a
reason, not a 4xx: the caller is asking a question, and a "no" is a
successful answer to it.

adjustedSizeUsd.description:
Present when the gates would silently shrink this order (Phoenix
add-headroom clamp). 6-decimal micro-USD, same scale as `sizeUsd`.

closeBps.description: For decrease orders: new close percentage in bps (0..10000). Omit to leave unchanged.

orderPda.description: Base58 PDA of the order to update.

priority.description: New Solana priority fee tier. Omit to leave unchanged.

oneOf.description: Per-type parameter update for advanced orders (ratchet / land-mine).

quote.description:
The re-quote this edit produced. Moving a stop changes what the preview
promises, and the number that matters when it fires is the last one
shown — so an update appends a snapshot rather than leaving the
original standing. Requires `side` / `orderType` / `underwriter` /
`marketMint` on the quote itself; this request addresses an existing
order by PDA and carries none of them.

Opaque for the same reason as the create path — see the note there.

sizeUsd.description: New size in USD. Omit to leave unchanged.

slippageBps.description: New slippage tolerance (bps). Omit to leave unchanged.

triggerPrice.description: New trigger price (oracle scale). Omit to leave unchanged.

wallet.description: Base58 wallet pubkey. Must match the JWT's wallet claim.

currentOiUsd.description:
Live current open interest (sum of `status='open'` lifecycles). Compare
against `rows`' last entry — divergence indicates indexer drift, not
arithmetic error in this endpoint.

OrderQuotePayload.description:
The client's `estimateOrderPnl` result plus the inputs it consumed.

Mirrors `order_quote_snapshots` one-for-one. Money fields are 6-decimal
micro-USD and prices are 1e9 oracle scale, matching `triggerPrice` on the
enclosing request — the client already works in those units at the call
site, so no rescaling happens on either side of the wire.

formulaVersion.description:
Bumped by the client whenever the quote formula changes, so a later
comparison never silently mixes two definitions of "quoted".

leg.description:
`"tp"` or `"sl"`. Taken from the leg the user was looking at rather
than re-inferred from `triggerCondition`, so the label matches the UI.

netCapitalMicro.description:
Absent when `getNetCapitalAtRisk` returned null and the quote fell back
to current collateral as its basis.

side.description:
Identity of the order being quoted. The create path takes these from
the enclosing request; the UPDATE path has no such fields (it addresses
an existing order by PDA), so re-quoting a moved stop supplies them
here. Ignored when the enclosing request already carries them.

PackPrizeOverlay.description:
What a pack pull's story needs from the desk, and what it hands back.

Serialized onto [`LifecycleResponse::pack_prize`] so the client's two PnL
calculators can stay on the real numbers while everything else renders the
story. See `rip_ev::backdate` for the arithmetic.

backdatedEntryPrice.description:
Where this pull's outcome would have started, if it had been a trade —
a real price the market really traded at [`backdated_opened_at`].

[`backdated_opened_at`]: PackPrizeOverlay::backdated_opened_at

backdatedOpenedAt.description: Unix seconds, of the bar that proved it.

pnlOffsetUsd.description:
`granted collateral − (stake − rip fee)`, fixed at the draw — the pull's own result.

★★★ SENT RATHER THAN DERIVED, because the client cannot derive it: the
granted collateral is a constant and `collateralUsd` on the wire is the
LIVE figure, which on a Phoenix seat drifts with the mark. One
definition, computed where the pull's own row can be read.

⚠⚠ ADD IT, NEVER RECOMPUTE FROM [`backdated_entry_price`].
`calculate_price_pnl` is `size × (mark − entry)/entry`, which reads
`size_usd` as the notional AT ENTRY; ours is the notional at open, so
that route is wrong by `M/p₀` — up to 15% at the bottom of the common
band on a 10× market, and plausible-looking at every size.

[`backdated_entry_price`]: PackPrizeOverlay::backdated_entry_price

ripFeeUsd.description: Part of the full purchase price, excluded from the position PnL basis.

stakeUsd.description:
Full purchase price. Subtract rip_fee_usd for the displayed PnL basis —
unless [`story_collateral_usd`] is set, which then IS the basis.

[`story_collateral_usd`]: PackPrizeOverlay::story_collateral_usd

storyCollateralUsd.description:
The collateral the pull shows, drawn with it. The displayed PnL basis
when present; `pnl_offset_usd` is already measured against it.

discountPending.description:
True when the wallet is bound to the partner but the on-chain
`set_wallet_fee_tier` leg has not succeeded yet — the partner should
retry POST /mobile/partner/register to activate the discount.

feeTierBps.description:
The fee tier currently ACTIVE on-chain — standard bps while the
on-chain flag leg is still pending (`discount_pending: true`).

creationSlot.description:
Solana slot at which the placement tx landed. The FE compares this
against the slot of its locally-cached Phoenix orderbook snapshot
before classifying a missing slot as "removed from book" — a
snapshot from a slot before this one couldn't have observed the
placement yet.

parentOrderPda.description:
Order PDA of the parent limit, when this is a close order (TP/SL/
Trailing) attached to a still-resting limit. The FE uses this
instead of the legacy `(market, side, profile)` heuristic to group
close orders under their parent. `None` for entry orders and for
close orders attached to an open position.

venueOrderState.description:
Per-venue resting state — Phoenix native carries (price_in_ticks,
order_sequence_number, initial_base_lots, remaining_base_lots,
trader_account_pda) so the FE can subscribe to the orderbook and
render live partial-fill progress. None for venues with no
resting state.

creationSlot.description:
Solana slot at which the placement tx landed. The FE compares this
against the slot of its locally-cached Phoenix orderbook snapshot
before deciding the order is "gone from book" — a snapshot from a
slot before this one couldn't have observed the placement, so we
must NOT classify a missing slot in that snapshot as a removal.

parentOrderPda.description:
Order PDA of the parent limit, when this is a close order (TP/SL/
Trailing) attached to a still-resting limit. The FE uses this
instead of the legacy `(market, side, profile)` heuristic to group
close orders under their parent — explicit links don't mis-attach
across markets/profiles. `None` for entry orders and for close
orders attached to an open position.

venueOrderState.description:
Per-venue runtime state of the resting order. For Phoenix-native
limits this carries `(price_in_ticks, order_sequence_number,
remaining_base_lots, trader_account_pda, …)` — the FE uses these
to scan the Phoenix orderbook account directly and render live
fill progress (X of Y filled). `None` for venues with no resting
state (Jupiter / Flash IOC fills, Phoenix native that hasn't
landed on the book yet).

PhoenixCrossSeatState.description:
Account-level state of one Phoenix cross-margin seat (subaccount 0).

In cross margin, collateral, margin and liquidation are properties of the
SEAT, not of any one position — so these are the only numbers that describe a
unified profile's risk, and no per-position figure substitutes for them.

Every field is a verbatim pass-through of Phoenix's `TraderView`. Imperial does
not recompute portfolio margin anywhere (that decision is in the plan: Phoenix is
authoritative and liquidates), and `risk_state` / `risk_tier` are surfaced as
Phoenix's own words rather than an Imperial health score.

Values are UI strings, matching `DirectVenueMetadata` and the rest of the Phoenix
surface. `None` means Phoenix did not report it — render it as unknown, never as
`0` (`feedback_never_render_unknown_balance_as_zero`).

accountCollateralUsd.description: Total deposited collateral on the seat.

effectiveCollateralUsd.description: Collateral plus discounted unrealised PnL — what actually backs positions.

initialMarginUsd.description:
Margin the open positions and resting orders already consume. Free margin is
`effectiveCollateral - initialMargin`; the order bot gates new unified opens
on exactly that subtraction.

liquidationPricesBySymbol.description:
Per-market liquidation price as PHOENIX computes it, keyed by its RAW symbol.

Imperial's own `compute_phoenix_liquidation_price` cannot be used on a cross
seat: it divides a per-position collateral figure into a per-position margin
requirement, and in cross neither exists — liquidation is a property of the
whole portfolio. Phoenix is the engine that actually liquidates, so its number
is the only correct one.

⚠ A price here does NOT promise which leg dies. Phoenix liquidates a cross seat
by closing whichever positions its engine picks; this is the level at which
THIS market becomes liable, not a guarantee it is the one that closes.

A `None` value means Phoenix quotes no price for that market — common, and not
an error (see [`PhoenixDecimalView::liquidation_ui`]). The KEY is still
present: these keys are how a consumer enumerates the markets on the seat,
including legs the position rows have not caught up with, so a market with no
price must stay in the map rather than vanish from it.

maxPositions.description:
Hard, unraisable ceiling on CONCURRENT positions. `max_positions` is
immutable and Phoenix has no resize instruction, so a power user who hits it
needs a fresh parent — surface it rather than letting them discover it as a
failed order.

openPositions.description: Slots currently occupied, i.e. distinct markets open on the seat.

riskTier.description:
Phoenix's own tier ladder (e.g. `"safe"`).

⚠ Phoenix liquidates a cross seat by closing whichever positions ITS engine
picks. We can surface the tier but cannot promise which leg dies — UI copy
must say so.

PhoenixMarkPrice.description:
Mid-price snapshot per Phoenix-raw symbol. The mid is `(best_bid + best_ask) / 2`
from the live orderbook WS feed, computed in `handle_text` and stored on the
snapshot. Empty until the WS connection has received its first orderbook
message; stale entries (no message in 60s) are filtered by `get_fresh`.

fetchedAt.description: Wall-clock time the most recent message landed, in milliseconds since epoch.

baseLotsDecimals.description:
Signed because Phoenix publishes negative values for some markets
(e.g. PUMP = -2). Mirrors `PhoenixMarketInfo.base_lots_decimals`.

isolatedOnly.description:
Phoenix rejects this market on the cross-margin seat, so unified-margin
profiles must not offer it. Meaningless for isolated trading.

logoUri.description: Display metadata from Phoenix; absent on older upstream responses.

maxLeverage.description: Max leverage from the first (smallest position) tier

maxSizeBaseLots.description: Max position size in base lots from the first tier

PhoenixMarketVolume.description:
Phoenix's own trailing-24h traded notional for one market. This is the
venue's total flow, not Imperial's share of it — the same `dayNtlVlm` the
trading header shows for the market you're looking at, exposed for every
market at once so the market selector can render a column of them. The
existing volume endpoint also exposes funding, USD OI and price statistics
from that same snapshot; existing volume consumers can ignore these fields.

fetchedAt.description: Wall-clock time the most recent message landed, in milliseconds since epoch.

fundingRate1hPct.description: Percent per hour, directly from Phoenix's market channel.

openInterestUsd.description: Phoenix publishes base units; converted to USD at the same snapshot's mark.

PledgeCapital.description: The pledge: how much of users' locked margin is lent to the hedge venue.

capitalShort.description:
Floor the pledgeable pool plus Imperial's float cannot reach. This is
the number a seed decision is actually made on.

pledge.description: What the rebalancer should have on the far side.

pledgeCap.description: The same, less what the winners may realize on Solana.

pledgeable.description: Locked margin the till leaves free to lend.

cumulativeFundingPayment.description:
Cumulative funding/interest paid (Phoenix funding + Jupiter borrow
rate + GMTrade funding). Signed: positive = paid out by trader.

cumulativePnl.description: Realized PnL accumulated up to and including this bucket. USD float.

cumulativeTakerFee.description:
Cumulative taker / order / venue execution fees across underwriters.
Excludes Imperial's platform fee and DEX swap fees.

unrealizedPnl.description:
Mark-to-market PnL of currently open positions at the time of the
request. **Only present on the last bucket** — historical
mark-to-market is not supported because we do not persist historical
mark prices. All earlier buckets serialize this field as `null`.

priority_fee.description:
Median Solana priority fee (micro-lamports per CU) observed across
recent blocks that touched the passthrough program. Polled every 30s
and clamped to a 500_000 ceiling so a stuck whale doesn't make the
suggestion useless. Field is `priority_fee` (snake_case) — this
endpoint predates the camelCase convention and stays as-is for
existing integrators.

marginMode.description:
`"isolated"` (the default) or `"unified"`. Unified routes this profile's
new positions onto a venue's shared collateral pool — Phoenix's
cross-margin seat, or Armada's cross margin account — see the "Cross
margin" guide in the API overview.

oneOf.description:
Present only when the mode constrains routing. The client must consume this
rather than deriving the lock from `margin_mode` itself, and must apply it
*before* the exclusion-override branches in `computeRoute` — sticky,
only-option and leverage-reach all deliberately override `excludedVenues`,
so an exclusion-encoded lock leaks through all three.

usdc.description:
USDC balance held in the profile's USDC ATA, in raw native units
(6-decimal — divide by `1_000_000` for whole USDC). `0` when the ATA
hasn't been created yet.

armadaParticipant.description:
Promotion preference, not a trading entitlement. True for any existing
allowlist row, including revoked rows; null if the lookup is unavailable.
The client must only invite a connected wallet on an explicit false.

betaVenues.description:
Venues in limited release that THIS WALLET has been granted, by wire
name — `["armada"]` for a wallet on the Armada private beta, `[]` for
everyone else.

Per wallet, not per profile: access is a statement about a person, and
the six profiles all belong to the same one.

A client must treat a venue that is absent here as one that does not
exist for this user — do not offer it, do not route to it, do not render
it in a venue picker. It is not `venueLock`'s inverse: `venueLock` is a
per-profile margin-mode consequence the user chose, this is an
entitlement the user cannot change.

⚠⚠ Applies to OPENS ONLY. A wallet with a position on a venue absent
from this list must still be able to close it, reduce it, and withdraw
from it, and every close path is keyed on the POSITION's venue rather
than on this field. Empty here is never a reason to hide an exit.

Empty on any error, so a client that fails closed and a server that
fails closed agree.

profiles.description:
Always six entries, indexed `0..5`, whether or not the profile has ever
been used.

RailsCapital.description: The rails the snapshot was computed under, recovered from its horizons.

inbound.description:
[`InboundRail::code`], or `None` when the stored horizons match no rail
this build knows — which is what a rail added on one side of a deploy
looks like, and is worth seeing rather than rounding away.

trailDistance.description: Fixed trail distance (`ratchet_size`, nano-USD) — absent for fib.

RateSource.description:
Provenance tag for a per-venue rate entry. Helps a bot author distinguish
live data from fallbacks without parsing free-form text.

profileIndex.description:
Sub-account index (0..5) being activated. Each profile activates
independently — bots farming across multiple subaccounts must register
each one before placing Phoenix orders from it.

wallet.description:
Owner wallet base58 pubkey. The activation is keyed on the profile PDA
derived from `wallet` + `profileIndex`.

RequiredDeposit.description:
Explicit upfront funding guidance for one venue at one (notional,
leverage). This is what must actually be available BEFORE the open —
unlike `costBreakdown`, whose borrow / expected-liq terms are lifecycle
EXPECTATIONS that are never reserved upfront. Deposit-first integrators
(prefund venues) should size deposits from `requiredDepositUsd`, not
`expectedCostUsd`.

degen.description:
Whether the venue's degen tier (leverage above its normal cap) applies
at this leverage — selects the degen minimum collateral.

depositSkimBps.description:
Imperial's flat deposit fee rate actually used (bps). Resolved from
the `wallet` query param's fee tier when present, else the Standard
tier — so partners see their real rate by passing `wallet`.

minPositionCollateralUsd.description:
The venue min-collateral floor applied (tier-selected, safety-padded).
Present only when the floor term is known for this venue.

requiredDepositUsd.description:
USD that must sit in the profile (prefund venues) or wallet
(self-funding venues) for the open to succeed, ceiled to the cent.
`max(collateral for the target leverage, venue min-collateral floor +
open-time fees)`, grossed up for Imperial's deposit skim.

upfrontFeeUsd.description:
Total upfront skim: Imperial's flat deposit fee + the venue's cash
open fee. Everything else in `costBreakdown` is NOT upfront.

venueOpenFeeUsd.description:
The venue's cash open fee at this notional (deducted from collateral
at open; reduces effective size/PnL, not the deposit).

oneOf.description:
Upfront funding required to open on this venue at
`min(desiredLeverage, maxLeverage)`.

RouteLoanSplit.description: The split-attachment shape carried on route candidates/results.

exclusionOverridden.description:
The winner is a venue the user excluded, but the router overrode the
exclusion because nothing else can serve the trade.

fundingModel.description:
How to fund an open on the winning `venue`. Branch on this BEFORE
opening: `self_funding` opens pull collateral from your wallet ATA inside
the open tx (do NOT pre-deposit); `prefund_v2` requires collateral staged
beforehand. See [`FundingModel`].

leverDownToLeverage.description:
Highest leverage a non-excluded venue could natively serve. Present
only on a leverage-driven exclusion override, where dropping to this
leverage would route the trade back onto an allowed venue.

marketsVersion.description:
Stable hash over the cross-venue market universe at request time. Two
responses with the same `marketsVersion` were computed against the same
market list — partners poll this to detect drift in the supported set
without re-snapshotting every venue. Set by the handler post-`compute_route`.

maxLeverage.description:
The winning venue's openable leverage cap. A per-market, fee-adjusted
constant — SIZE-INDEPENDENT (identical at any `notional`), so don't
scale it by trade size. On prefund venues it already folds every
open-time deduction; orders sized at or below it clear the venue's
on-chain init-leverage check.

oneOf.description:
Upfront funding required on the winning venue at the EFFECTIVE leverage
(`clampedMaxLeverage` when the route clamped, else `desiredLeverage`).
Set by the handler post-`compute_route`.

marksComplete.description:
Whether every market in the book had a usable mark when the floors were
computed. A floor computed on a partial book understates it, and after
the fact there is no way to tell — which is why it is stored.

unpriced.description:
Markets the api's own feed could find no tail or no venue parameters
for. A non-empty list means the recomputed floor below understates
itself, so the drift check is advisory rather than binding.

SolanaCapital.description: The Solana side: whether the vault can pay a close the moment it happens.

arriving.description: What closes are waiting on a return hop for.

distance.description: Balance less floor. Negative is the dollar figure of "arriving".

freeCollateral.description:
Protected local cash. New snapshots protect escrow and explicit reserve
overrides; older models also protected all free customer collateral.

lockedIm.description:
Users' locked initial margin: the lendable pool, till included.
`None` when `till_ratio` is zero, which is the one case the identity
`till = ratio × locked_im` cannot be inverted through.

lockedOnSolana.description: Locked margin that has NOT been pledged to the hedge venue.

payoutsDue.description: Actual pending payout cash beyond already protected collateral.

realizable.description: What the winners could realize inside one outbound hop.

till.description: The share of locked margin held back so closes pay instantly.

tillRatio.description: The ratio that till was computed at, echoed from the model.

withdrawalOnDemand.description: Whether unused settled collateral can be bridged until requested.

oneOf.description:
Pre-sweep snapshot of the profile's tokenized residue. Present whenever
the response had something to act on — useful for the bot to confirm
post-close what was reclaimed. Token amounts are in their respective
native scales (SOL: lamports / 1e9, BTC: 1e8, ETH: 1e8).

status.description:
`"clean"` — nothing to sweep (no token-form residue on the profile).
`"queued"` — a sweep was already triggered recently; this call is a
no-op until the lock expires (~10s).
`"swept"` — the operator submitted sweep instructions to bring residual
WSOL/WBTC/WETH back to the user wallet as USDC.

TouchBookView.description:
Standing inventory and capital usage for this market, µUSD. Absent when
the book account hasn't been read yet.

eCrashUsd.description: Net exposure to the downside tail, µUSD.

eMeltupUsd.description: Net exposure to the upside tail, µUSD.

fairMarkLiabilityUsd.description: Probability-weighted payout liability at the last mark walk.

rawReserveUsd.description: Worst-case net payout reserved against LP withdrawals.

stressUsageUsd.description:
Largest stressed payout across the on-chain scenario grid. This is the
numerator used by the market's `portfolioCapBps` capacity gate.

TouchConfigView.description:
The market's on-chain `TouchConfig`, verbatim. Every pricing input the
program uses is here, so a client can reproduce an ask offline; most
integrators only need `cohortQuantumSecs` / `cohortWindowSecs` (expiry),
`minPayoutUsd` / `maxPayoutUsd` (ticket bounds), and `floorBps` /
`ceilBps` (the band a quotable ask must fall strictly inside).

alphaBps.description: Base spread over fair value, bps.

ceilBps.description: Maximum quotable ask, bps of payout (10000 = parity).

cohortQuantumSecs.description:
Cohort boundary spacing, seconds. An open snaps DOWN to a multiple of
this — buying at 13:23 with a 3600s quantum joins the 13:00 cohort.

cohortWindowSecs.description:
Contract lifetime, seconds — the tenor. Expiry is the cohort open plus
this. One tenor per market; a market's tenor never changes.

eScaleUsd.description: Inventory normalizer, µUSD — the exposure at which the skew is 1×.

fD1e6.description: First-passage table: barrier distance in σ units, 1e6 scale.

fP1e6.description: First-passage table: touch probability at each `fD1e6`, 1e6 scale.

floorBps.description:
Minimum quotable ask, bps of payout. An ask that clamps to this is not
a real price — the program refuses the open.

gamma1e6.description: Convexity coefficient on the inventory term, 1e6 scale.

kImplied1e3.description: Implied-vol multiplier applied to the blended σ, 1e3 scale.

minImpliedDtSecs.description: Floor on the time-to-expiry used for pricing, seconds.

perBarrierCapBps.description: Per-barrier exposure cap, bps of pool NAV.

portfolioCapBps.description: Whole-book exposure cap, bps of pool NAV.

sigmaMaxAgeSecs.description: Staleness bound on `vol.postTs`. Past this the market stops quoting.

w1e6.description: Short-σ weight at each `wTauSecs` breakpoint, 1e6 scale.

wTauSecs.description: Term-structure breakpoints (seconds) for the σ blend weights.

TouchDealRow.description: A quotable barrier and its indicative ask.

askBps.description:
Indicative ask, bps of payout. `premium = payout × askBps / 10000`.
Marginal (quoted at payout → 0), so a large ticket fills slightly
wider — size your premium budget above this, don't send it as the
exact price.

barrier1e9.description: Barrier price, 1e9 scale — send this as `triggerPrice` to buy.

TouchMarketRow.description:
One tradeable touch market. Tenors are separate markets — `SOL` at 5m and
`SOL` at 24h are two rows with different `marketId` and
`config.cohortWindowSecs`.

halted.description:
True when the market is not quoting — halted on-chain, σ stale, or the
operator kill switch is engaged. Open contracts still settle.

marketId.description:
Stable market id. Also derives the Market PDA you send as
`marketMint` on `POST /mobile/orders`.

spotPrice1e9.description: Live index price, 1e9 scale. Barriers are quoted against this.

symbol.description:
On-chain market symbol, e.g. `SOLTOUCH`. The underlying is the part
before `TOUCH`; several markets share it, one per tenor.

TouchVolView.description:
Live volatility state, posted by the vol keeper from a licensed IV feed.
Quoting stops when `postTs` is older than `config.sigmaMaxAgeSecs`.

anchorSpot1e9.description: Spot at the last σ post, 1e9 scale.

navSnapshotUsd.description:
Underwriting pool NAV at the last post, µUSD — the base the
`perBarrierCapBps` / `portfolioCapBps` limits are taken against.

postTs.description: Unix seconds of the last σ post. Zero means never posted.

sigmaTouchFloor1e9.description: Floor the blended σ is clamped up to, 1e9 scale.

widenMult1e3.description: Risk-widening multiplier currently applied to σ, 1e3 scale.

TpSlOrderResponse.description: Unified TP/SL order response - represents orders from both Jupiter native and Imperial passthrough

closeBps.description:
Decrease-only close percentage in basis points (10000 = 100%). The
on-chain Order carries this so the program can apply it to live
position size at execution; surfacing it here lets the FE render the
user's chosen percentage without falling back to the
`orderSizeUsd / positionSizeUsd` ratio (which drifts above 100% when
the parent limit fills slightly under-size). `None` for legacy rows
created before the indexer started splatting `close_bps` into
`passthrough_orders.order_data`.

dcaStartAt.description:
Optional delayed-start unix ts (0/None = no delay). Immutable after
creation, so the indexer's `order_data` is an authoritative source —
unlike `dca_last_leg_timestamp`, this never needs WS enrichment.

oneOf.description:
Imperial Armada. Keyed on the UNDERWRITER's own book, not on the hedge
venue behind it: one Armada byte fans out to several user-facing venues
and this rate is Imperial's, charged identically whichever venue carries
the hedge. The hedge venue's own rate is not served here — it belongs to
that venue and lives on `/armada/orderbook`.

UserErrorDetails.description:
Additive, user-safe error metadata shared by HTTP, WebSocket, history, and
notification surfaces. Raw provider/program text must never be copied into
this structure.

retryAfterSecs.description:
How long a client should wait before trying the SAME request again, when
the refusal is a "not yet" rather than a "no".

⚠ The machine-readable half of a wait. The seconds are also in
`message`, and a client must never parse them back out of it: that text
is English prose, it is the half we intend to translate, and a client
keying on it would break on the first locale. Absent means "we do not
know how long", which is not the same as zero.

oneOf.description: Validated live Armada loan policy. Absent means borrowing is unavailable.

borrowHourlyPct.description:
Hourly borrow/funding cost as a percent of notional. JLP-style venues charge
borrow on utilized liquidity; CLOBs run zero-sum funding and pass ~0.

oneOf.description:
Side-specific override for `borrow_hourly_pct`. Required for GMTrade where long
and short pay different combined funding+borrow rates. Negative entries mean the
venue pays the trader on that side; cost computation clamps to 0.

degenLeverageThreshold.description:
Leverage above which the venue's degen tier (and its minimum
collateral) applies.

minDegenPositionCollateralUsd.description:
Venue minimum collateral (USD) for degen-tier opens (leverage above
`degen_leverage_threshold`).

minPositionCollateralUsd.description:
Venue minimum collateral (USD) for normal-tier opens, conservative
`max(target custody, collateral custody)`. Prefund venues only.

mmr.description:
Maintenance margin ratio (fraction of notional). Liquidation triggers when
residual collateral falls below `mmr × notional`.

openDeductionRate.description:
Total size-scaled rate the venue deducts from collateral at open time
(the same rate folded into `max_leverage`, including any currently
active volatility fee). Prefund venues only — drives `requiredDeposit`.

longBorrowRatePerHourPercent.description:
Hourly borrow rate in percent. Always non-negative — the side holding
the position pays this regardless of funding direction. Set even when
only one side borrows (Jupiter longs pay borrow on the long custody;
shorts on the short/USDC custody — both sides populated).

longFundingRatePerHourPercent.description:
Hourly funding rate in percent (`0.04` = 0.04%). Sign convention is
uniform across every venue this API serves: **positive long rate ⇒
longs pay shorts** (i.e. shorts receive); negative ⇒ shorts pay longs.
GMTrade rates are passed through raw from the venue WS feed (which
already follows that convention); Phoenix exposes a single signed
rate so the short-side value is the negation of the long-side. For
Jupiter this field is `None` — that venue charges borrow fees
instead, see `*_borrow_rate_*`.

VenueLock.description:
A whitelist, not a blacklist: `excludedVenues` cannot express "only Phoenix"
without also encoding every future venue we add.

venues.description:
The only venues this profile may OPEN on while the lock is in force.
Closes, reduces, and cancels always route to the position's own venue.

fetchedAtUnixMs.description:
Wall-clock time the underlying snapshot was last refreshed, in
milliseconds since epoch. For Phoenix this is the WS message
timestamp.
