bearer_jwt.description: JWT issued via `/mobile/connect` + `/mobile/exchange`. The wallet claim in the JWT must match the `wallet` field in each trading request body.

info.description:
Imperial is a perpetual futures router on Solana — a single passthrough program that brokers
trades across multiple underlying perp venues (Jupiter, Phoenix, GMTrade, …).
This HTTP API is the surface third-party bots and integrators use to authenticate, submit
orders, and read public on-chain state.

## Authentication

Trading endpoints are JWT-gated. The flow:

1. `POST /mobile/connect` — sign `imperial:mobile-connect:{wallet}:{nonce}` with your Solana
   keypair and post `{wallet, message, signature}`. `{nonce}` must be a **current Unix
   timestamp** — seconds or milliseconds (e.g. `Date.now()`), **not** a random value. It is
   rejected if it is more than 5 minutes old or more than 60 seconds in the future, and each
   nonce may be used only once. Response: a one-time `code`.

   Note: on failure this endpoint returns an opaque `401 {"error":"Failed to generate mobile
   session"}` for *any* underlying cause — bad signature, malformed/expired nonce, or replay —
   so an unexpected 401 with a valid signature almost always means the nonce is not a fresh
   timestamp. (A `400 {"error":"Invalid message format"}` specifically means the signed string
   didn't match the `imperial:mobile-connect:{wallet}:{nonce}` prefix.)
2. `POST /mobile/exchange` — exchange the `code` for `{jwt, expires_at}`. The code expires in
   5 minutes and can only be redeemed once.
3. Send trading requests with `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`. The JWT's wallet claim must match
   the `wallet` field in every request body.
4. `POST /mobile/revoke` — revoke the JWT when you're done (e.g. bot shutdown, key rotation).

The JWT is a Solana-signature-anchored delegation: holding it is equivalent to letting the
operator place orders from the associated wallet's profiles. Treat it like an API key — copy
it once, store it securely, and revoke it if compromised.

Multi-wallet bots (e.g. fan-out traders): each wallet owner independently completes the flow
on their own dashboard and shares their JWT with the bot operator. The bot then holds N tokens
and calls the API in parallel, one request per wallet. Any wallet owner can revoke their token
anytime without affecting the others.

## Partner program

Integration partners with a partner code register each trading wallet once to receive their
discounted fee tier and volume attribution:

1. Complete the authentication flow above for the wallet.
2. `POST /mobile/partner/register` with `{ "code": "<YOUR-CODE>" }` and the wallet's JWT.
   The response confirms the discounted fee rate (bps) and the on-chain transaction that
   activated it. Registration is one-time per wallet and idempotent — on a `503`, retry the
   same call.
3. `GET /mobile/partner/registration` — verify a wallet's registration status at any time.

Register a wallet **before** its first order; the discount applies to fees charged from that
point on. A wallet binds to one partner code permanently (first code wins).

## Builder codes

Third-party frontends and bots ("builders") can charge their users an additional fee on top
of Imperial's standard fee by attaching their builder code to orders:

1. Pass `builderCode` on `POST /mobile/orders` (or on every leg of `POST /mobile/orders/batch`
   — all legs must carry the same code, or none). The code's fixed bps rate is charged on the
   same base as the standard flat fee, on **both** the open and close legs. Codes are
   case-insensitive; unknown or deactivated codes are rejected with `400`.
2. Preview the fee: `GET /trade-preview?...&builderCode=<CODE>` adds `builderFeeUsd` and
   `builderFeeBps` to each side's fee estimate, folded into `totalFeesUsd`.
3. `GET /mobile/builder/summary?code=<CODE>` — accrued, paid, and claimable builder fees plus
   the latest payouts. The code itself is the credential; no JWT required.

Accrued fees are paid out periodically to the builder's registered payout wallet. Disclose
the fee to your users in your app — the charge is per-order and only applies to orders that
carry your code.

## Imperial points

`GET /mobile/points` (JWT required) returns the wallet's Imperial points for the active
season — the same on-chain balance the Imperial homepage displays. Points are credited in
weekly batches at each week's close, so the figure updates weekly rather than per-trade.

## Rate limits

Unified limit: **600 requests/minute sustained, burst of 120**. Keyed per-wallet when a valid
JWT is present, else per-IP. Exceeding the budget returns `429 Too Many Requests` with a
`Retry-After` header and `{ "error": "rate_limited", "retry_after_seconds": N }` body. The
`/health`, `/ws`, and Telegram webhook endpoints are not rate limited.

## WebSockets

Two endpoints. Both are unauthenticated and exempt from the rate limiter.

### `GET /ws` — wallet-scoped position/order stream

Subscribe by wallet — single `wallet`, or a `wallets` array to multiplex a fleet over ONE
socket. By default you get coalesced invalidation triggers only. Add `"positionState": true`
to also have the full position rows pushed (so you never poll `/positions`), and
`"tradeEvents": true` for typed settled close events (so you never poll `/trades` at close).

```json
{ "type": "subscribe", "wallet": "<base58-pubkey>", "positionState": true }
{ "type": "subscribe", "wallets": ["<pk1>", "<pk2>"], "tradeEvents": true }
```

Every `subscribe` REPLACES the connection's whole subscription set (the single-`wallet` form
is a set of one — identical to the historical behavior), so a fleet client just resends its
full roster when wallets change; `"wallets": []` clears and there is no separate unsubscribe
message. Caps: 200 wallets per connection; `positionState` is honored up to 25 subscribed
wallets (each open wallet costs a periodic `/positions` computation; the per-second re-marks
between are served from a local price cache) — beyond that the
server sends `{ "type": "error", "code": "position_state_wallet_limit", "limit": 25 }` once
and disables it for the connection (triggers and `tradeEvents` still flow). Every
wallet-scoped frame carries a top-level `wallet` field for demuxing.

- `{ "type": "position_state", "seq": N, "positions": [ ... ] }` — **opt-in** (`positionState:
  true`). The full `/positions` response rows (identical shape: `markPrice`, `pnlUsd`,
  `pnlPercent`, `collateralUsd`, `ourLiquidationPriceUsd`, `sizeUsd`, `entryPrice`, `side`,
  `status`, and any attached `stopLossPrice`/`takeProfitPrice`). `seq` is a per-connection
  monotonic counter for ordering / gap detection across a reconnect. Cadence:
  - one frame immediately on `subscribe` (snapshot) — this doubles as the subscribe ack;
    there is no separate `subscribed` frame. The snapshot may be `positions: []` if the
    wallet is currently flat — that's a valid frame, not an error.
  - a frame on every position change (open / close / SL-TP fire / liquidation);
  - while a position is open, a re-marked frame ~1×/s so live PnL / mark / liq track without
    polling. **While the wallet is flat, no periodic frames are sent** (the socket goes quiet
    until the next change), so an empty frame followed by silence means "no open position".
- `{ "type": "positions_updated", "wallet": "<pk>" }` — the coalesced invalidation trigger,
  always sent (also alongside `position_state` when opted in). Clients consuming
  `position_state` can ignore it.
- `{ "type": "orders_updated", "wallet": "<pk>" }` — fired on order creation, execution, and
  cancellation. Refetch `/orders` for the unified view, or
  `/passthrough/users/{wallet}/orders` for the passthrough subset only.
- `{ "type": "order_rejected", "wallet": "<pk>", "actionId": "<uuid>", "reasonCode":
  "<code>" }` — a specific order was rejected on-chain.
- `{ "type": "position_closed" | "position_liquidated", "wallet": "<pk>", "lifecycleId":
  "<uuid>", "closedAt": <unix-seconds>, "trade": { ...LifecycleResponse } }` — **opt-in**
  (`tradeEvents: true`). Fired once per closed lifecycle, only after the close has fully
  SETTLED (every closing leg's sweep finalized), carrying the same row `/trades` would
  return — `netCashPnlUsd`, `totalFeesUsd`, `fees`, per-action `userReceived`, `closedAt` —
  so no close-time `/trades` re-poll is needed. Note the ordering: the instant the close
  lands you get `positions_updated` (and a `position_state` frame in which the position is
  gone); the typed event follows seconds later when settlement completes. Dedupe by
  `lifecycleId` — delivery is at-least-once across reconnects.

Ping/pong keepalive: send `{ "type": "ping" }`, receive `{ "type": "pong" }`. On reconnect,
re-`subscribe`; the snapshot `position_state` re-syncs current state (there is no server-side
replay buffer for missed intermediate frames).

### `GET /ws/market` — public market-data stream

Replaces polling on `/funding-rates`, `/mark-prices`, and `/phoenix/depth`. Each push carries
the full payload, so clients never have to refetch. On every successful `subscribe_*` the
server immediately pushes the current cached snapshot before tracking diffs — late
subscribers don't have to wait a publisher tick.

Subscribe / unsubscribe messages:

```json
{ "type": "subscribe_funding_rates" }
{ "type": "subscribe_mark_prices" }
{ "type": "subscribe_phoenix_depth" }                      // all symbols
{ "type": "subscribe_phoenix_depth", "symbols": ["SOL"] }  // filtered
{ "type": "unsubscribe_funding_rates" }
{ "type": "unsubscribe_mark_prices" }
{ "type": "unsubscribe_phoenix_depth" }
{ "type": "ping" }
```

Server-pushed events:

- `{ "type": "funding_rate_update", "symbol": "SOL", "venue": "phoenix" | "jupiter" |
  "gmtrade", "source": <RateSource>, "longFundingRatePerHourPercent": <f64|null>,
  "shortFundingRatePerHourPercent": <f64|null>, "longBorrowRatePerHourPercent": <f64|null>,
  "shortBorrowRatePerHourPercent": <f64|null> }` — same shape as a per-venue entry on
  `/funding-rates`. The `source` discriminator carries provenance (live vs. fallback);
  filter on it the same way you would in the REST response.
- `{ "type": "mark_price_update", "symbol": "SOL", "venue": "phoenix" | "jupiter"
  | "gmtrade" | "index", "source": <PriceSource>, "price": <f64>, "fetchedAtUnixMs":
  <i64> }`. The `venue: "index"` entries (`source: "pyth_lazer"`) are **the price Imperial
  marks positions with** — the same feed that drives `/positions`/`position_state`
  `markPrice`, PnL, and liquidation monitoring. Chart, PnL, and liq logic can all read this
  one number (≤1 Hz per symbol, change-gated); the other venue entries are each venue's own
  oracle and may differ slightly.
- `{ "type": "phoenix_depth_update", "symbol": "SOL", "snapshot": <DepthSnapshot> }` —
  the `symbol` here is the **Phoenix-raw** symbol (`GOLD` rather than `XAU`), matching
  what `/phoenix/depth` returns.

Funding sign convention: `longFundingRatePerHourPercent > 0` means longs pay shorts.
Phoenix's short rate is the negation of its long rate (single-pool perp); GMTrade reports
both sides independently. Funding fields are `null` for venues that only expose borrow
rates (Jupiter) — populated borrow fields are non-negative regardless of side.

Symbols are canonical (`SOL`, `BTC`, `XAU`) on `funding_rate_update` and `mark_price_update`;
`phoenix_depth_update` uses Phoenix-raw symbols (`SOL`, `GOLD`, …). Translate accordingly.

## Order types

The `orderType` field on `/mobile/orders` takes a numeric code:

| Code | Name             | Notes                                                   |
|-----:|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
|    0 | Market           | `triggerPrice` ignored                                  |
|    1 | Limit            | Requires `triggerPrice`                                 |
|    2 | StopLimit        | Requires `triggerPrice`                                 |
|    3 | LandMine         | Requires `triggerPrice`, `extraData.waitPrice`, `waitDuration` |
|    4 | Ratchet          | Requires `extraData.worstPrice`, `ratchetSize`          |
|    6 | RatchetEntry     | Same extras as Ratchet                                  |
|    9 | Dca              | Requires `extraData.dcaStartPrice`, `dcaEndPrice`, `dcaNumLegs` |
|   10 | FibRatchet       | Same extras as Ratchet                                  |
|   11 | FibRatchetEntry  | Same extras as Ratchet                                  |
|   12 | DcaClose         | Requires `extraData.dcaCloseStartPrice`, `dcaCloseEndPrice`, `dcaCloseNumLegs` |
|   13 | DcaTimeClose     | Requires `extraData.dcaCloseIntervalSeconds`, `dcaCloseNumLegs` |
|   14 | DcaRatchetClose  | Requires `extraData.dcaCloseNumLegs`, `dcaCloseRatchetSize` |
|   15 | DcaTime          | Requires `extraData.dcaIntervalSeconds`, `dcaNumLegs`   |
|   16 | DcaRatchet       | Requires `extraData.dcaNumLegs`, `dcaRatchetSize`       |

`underwriter`: 0 = Jupiter, 2 = Phoenix, 3 = GMTrade, 5 = Pairs, 6 = Imperial Touch,
7 = Imperial Armada. Wire format mirrors `passthrough_client::Underwriter`. Bytes 1 and 4
were Flash Trade and Flash Trade V2; that venue has SHUT DOWN and both are rejected on
create. They still appear on historical orders and positions.
`side`: 0 = long, 1 = short.
`action`: 0 = Increase, 1 = Decrease.

Armada uses `underwriter: 7`. `requestedHedgeVenue` is an optional execution
constraint: `0` (the default) lets Armada choose its hedge route; `1` binds to
Armada's current hedge route. Values `2` and `3` are reserved and rejected.
A binding route is never silently substituted. On every other underwriter,
this field must be `0`.

Not every venue takes every order type. Touch (`underwriter: 6`) accepts only `0`, `1`, and
`2`, and reinterprets several fields — see "Imperial Touch" below. Pairs (`underwriter: 5`)
and Armada (`underwriter: 7`) reject the DCA family. A Armada **open** must also carry a
non-zero `slippageBps`: nothing on chain can verify the price Imperial reports for an
off-Solana fill, so the user's own band is the entire bound and `0` means unbounded. Closes
are exempt so a must-close is never blocked.

## Price scales

`triggerPrice` — and every price inside `extraData` (`worstPrice`, `waitPrice`, DCA
start/end/limit prices) — is **always oracle scale (1e9)**: `price × 1e9`, on every venue.

One exception: on a **touch buyback** (`underwriter: 6`, `action: 1`) `triggerPrice` is not a
price at all — it carries `positionId + 1` as a plain integer. See "Imperial Touch".

`marketPrice` on `/mobile/orders` (and `price` on `/mobile/orders/collateral`) is
**per-underwriter**: it is forwarded to each venue's on-chain slippage check in that
venue's native encoding. Sending the wrong scale makes market orders fail the slippage
guard (or pass it vacuously). Example encodings for SOL at $64.94:

| Underwriter       | Scale                                  | Encoded value |
|-------------------|----------------------------------------|---------------|
| 0 Jupiter         | micro-USD, `price × 1e6`               | `64940000`    |
| 2 Phoenix         | micro-USD, `price × 1e6`               | `64940000`    |
| 3 GMTrade         | oracle scale, `price × 1e9`            | `64940000000` |
| 5 Imperial Pairs  | micro-USD, `price × 1e6`               | `64940000`    |
| 6 Imperial Touch  | ignored — send `0`                     | `0`           |
| 7 Imperial Armada| micro-USD, `price × 1e6`               | `64940000`    |

⚠ On Armada (7) this field is not only a slippage reference. It becomes the request's
`expected_price` on `imperial_sunrise` (rescaled to that program's 1e9 units), which is the
value BOTH on-chain price bands measure against — the user's `slippageBps` band and the
config's `maxFavourableBps`, the latter being Imperial's own protection. A `marketPrice` far
from the venue's mark is refused after the hedge rather than filled, so send a live one.

GMTrade uses 1e9 because micro-USD truncates
sub-$0.001 assets (BONK ≈ $0.0000074 → `7` at 1e6) and collapses the slippage band to zero.

## Maker orders (Phoenix-native)

By default a `Limit` (or `PrivateTpSl`) order on `underwriter = 2` (Phoenix) is **not** a
maker order: the API rewrites it to `StopLimit` and the keeper triggers an IOC market fill
when the price is reached. To rest a genuine maker order on Phoenix's CLOB, set
`phoenixNative: true` on the create request. This is the only supported maker path; no other
venue rests natively today.

Semantics when `phoenixNative` is set:

- **Eligibility.** Honored only for `underwriter = 2` AND either `orderType = 1` (Limit) with
  `action = 0` (Increase), or `orderType = 5` (PrivateTpSl). Ignored for any other shape. A
  Phoenix-native `Limit` with `action = 1` (Decrease) is rejected on-chain — express
  close-side resting orders as `PrivateTpSl` instead.
- **Always post-only.** The order is placed with Phoenix `PostOnly` and slide disabled, so it
  never takes liquidity. There is no separate `postOnly`/`maker` field — it's implied. An
  order that would cross the spread is **rejected** (not repriced): submit a non-crossing
  `triggerPrice`, or use `orderType = 0` (Market) for taker fills.
- **Price/size scale is unchanged.** `triggerPrice` stays oracle scale (1e9), `sizeUsd` stays
  6-decimal; the order bot converts to Phoenix ticks/base-lots internally.
- **No in-place update.** `/mobile/orders/update` against a native order returns
  `success: false` ("native limit-order updates not supported"). To re-price or re-size,
  cancel via `/mobile/orders/cancel` and place a new one. A pre-fill cancel refunds the
  unfilled portion of the Imperial fee.
- **Fills.** Partial fills are supported — the order stays open with reduced remaining size
  until fully filled. A resting maker order fills when a taker crosses it, so it has no
  transaction of its own; poll `/orders` / `/positions` (or watch the `/ws` user channel)
  rather than treating placement as the fill. The order's status moves `resting → filled` in
  place; `action` never changes.

Default routing (unset / `false`) deliberately avoids the native path — it dodges a class of
indexer/orderbook-watcher edge cases that have stranded collateral. Opt in only if you need
true resting CLOB orders (e.g. maker-fee strategies).

## Imperial Touch (binary options)

Imperial Touch is a separate product on the same order surface: one-touch binaries, not perps.
You buy a fixed **payout** for an up-front **premium**, and the contract resolves on its own.

- **Touch** (`side: 0`) pays the full payout if spot reaches the barrier at any point before
  expiry — one tick is enough, and the payout is locked in the moment it happens.
- **No-Touch** (`side: 1`) pays if spot never reaches the barrier before expiry.

Either way the premium is the entire risk: there is no liquidation, no margin, no funding, and
no collateral to reclaim. A losing contract simply expires worthless.

### Markets and tenors

`GET /api/v1/touch/markets` lists every market with its live spot, on-chain pricing config,
volatility state, and standing book inventory.

**Each tenor is its own market.** `SOL` at 5 minutes and `SOL` at 24 hours are two rows with
different `marketId`, distinguished by `config.cohortWindowSecs`. The `symbol` carries the
underlying as a prefix (`SOLTOUCH` → `SOL`), so group rows by that prefix and pick the tenor
you want. Addressing a touch order by bare `symbol` resolves to the **lowest `marketId`** for
the asset — which is a specific tenor, not a preference. Always send `marketMint` (the market's
PDA) so you get the tenor you intended.

`halted: true` means the market is not quoting — halted on-chain, its σ feed went stale past
`config.sigmaMaxAgeSecs`, or the operator kill switch is engaged. Open contracts still settle
normally while halted.

### Expiry is a shared cohort clock, not a per-contract timer

Contracts do not expire N seconds after you buy. Every open joins the current **cohort**: the
open time snaps DOWN to a `config.cohortQuantumSecs` boundary, and expiry is one full
`config.cohortWindowSecs` after that boundary. With a 1h quantum and a 24h window, a contract
bought at 13:23 opens at 13:00 and expires at 13:00 the next day — 23h37m later, not 24h.
Everyone in a cohort shares both endpoints exactly.

One exception: an open landing in the final `min(75s, window/4)` of a window joins the NEXT
cohort instead (a forward start — price action before that window begins never counts toward
it). So a contract bought near the tail gets a full-length window that hasn't started yet.

Read `openTs` / `expiryTs` off the position rather than deriving them, and don't assume
"bought now" means "expires now + tenor".

### Pricing

`GET /api/v1/touch/deals` is the fast path: a ranked grid of quotable barriers at ±1/2/3/5/8%
from spot, both sides, each with an indicative `askBps` (bps of payout — `premium = payout ×
askBps / 10000`). Barriers the pool won't quote are already filtered out. Take a row, choose a
payout, submit.

You never have to price client-side, because **consent is a budget, not a price**. You send the
maximum premium you'll pay; the fill debits the live ask, and the difference is refunded, not
spent. So quote drift between reading a deal and the fill landing is absorbed by the budget
instead of rejecting the order. The homepage stages the displayed ask plus 100 bps of slack.
If the live ask still exceeds your budget nothing is bought and you get `TouchQuoteMoved` —
re-read and retry.

Asks are marginal (quoted at payout → 0) and skew with the pool's standing inventory
(`book.eCrashUsd` / `book.eMeltupUsd`), so a large ticket fills a little wider than the quote.
`config.minPayoutUsd` / `maxPayoutUsd` bound the ticket. To reproduce the full model offline,
`config` carries every input the program uses; `imperial_core::touch` is the reference
implementation and `clients/homepage/src/lib/touch/math.ts` mirrors it.

### Buying a contract

`POST /mobile/orders` with `underwriter: 6` and `action: 0`. Touch reuses the perp order
record, so several fields carry **different meanings** — this mapping is the contract:

| Field              | Meaning for a touch buy                                                |
|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `underwriter`      | `6`                                                                    |
| `marketMint`       | the touch market's PDA (derive from `marketId`; prefer this to `symbol`) |
| `side`             | `0` = Touch, `1` = No-Touch                                            |
| `action`           | `0` — a binary has no close leg                                        |
| `orderType`        | `0` (Market). `1`/`2` rest until the barrier prints; nothing else is accepted |
| `triggerPrice`     | **the barrier**, 1e9 oracle scale                                      |
| `sizeUsd`          | **the payout**, µUSD (6-decimal)                                       |
| `collateralAmount` | **the premium budget** — your max, µUSD. Must cover ≥1¢ per $1 of payout |
| `slippageBps`      | unused — send `0`. Consent rides the budget, not a price band          |

```json
{
  "wallet": "<wallet>",
  "marketMint": "<touch market PDA>",
  "underwriter": 6,
  "side": 0,
  "orderType": 0,
  "action": 0,
  "triggerCondition": 0,
  "triggerPrice": 77550000000,
  "sizeUsd": 25000000,
  "collateralAmount": 2200000,
  "slippageBps": 0,
  "profileIndex": 0
}
```

That buys a Touch at $77.55 paying $25, spending at most $2.20. Ratchets, land mines, DCA, and
TP/SL have no meaning on a binary and are rejected — the barrier *is* the contract.

### Selling back early

A contract can be sold back to the pool before expiry at the live bid. Same endpoint,
`action: 1`, and the field overloading changes again:

| Field              | Meaning for a buyback                                                   |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `action`           | `1`                                                                     |
| `orderType`        | `0` (Market) — fires synchronously, so the response carries the fill     |
| `triggerPrice`     | **`positionId + 1`** — an id, NOT a price, and NOT 1e9-scaled (id 0 → `1`) |
| `sizeUsd`          | the position's `payoutUsd`, echoed exactly as `/touch/positions` returned it |
| `collateralAmount` | **min-refund floor**, µUSD — `0` accepts any quotable bid                |

Echo `sizeUsd` byte-for-byte from the position row; it is cross-checked against on-chain state
before the buyback fires, and a re-derived value that rounds differently is refused.

Buyback is not always available. Once the barrier is swept or the cohort has expired, the
position belongs to settlement — you get `TouchSettlesAtExpiry` and should simply wait for the
payout.

### Settlement

Automatic. A keeper settles each cohort at expiry and a Touch that hits pays out the moment it
is swept — there is nothing to call and no close leg to submit. Watch `status` on
`/touch/positions`: `open` → `settled` (expired, `won` tells you the outcome) or
`bought_back`. `payoutPaidUsd` is what the wallet actually received: the payout on a win, the
refund on a buyback, `0` on a loss. Proceeds land in the profile's USDC balance — no residue
sweep is needed.

### Touch-specific error codes

Alongside the usual codes, `errorCode` may be:

- `TouchQuoteMoved` — the live ask outran your premium budget (or the bid fell below your
  min-refund floor). Nothing traded; re-read the quote and retry.
- `TouchBarrierSwept` — that barrier has already been touched in the live cohort, so it is no
  longer sellable. Pick another barrier or the next cohort.
- `TouchSettlesAtExpiry` — buyback refused because settlement now owns the position. Wait.
- `PositionAlreadyClosed` — already settled or bought back.

### Not covered by the perp surface

Touch positions appear **only** on `/touch/positions`. They are absent from `/positions`,
`/trades`, `/orders`, `/order-history`, `/stats/*`, and both WebSocket streams — all of which
are perp-only. There is no push channel for touch yet, so poll `/touch/positions`; once per
few seconds is plenty given cohort-quantized expiry.

## Subaccounts (profiles)

Every wallet has six implicit subaccounts indexed `0..5`. Balances and positions don't mix
across them. There is no "create subaccount" call — the on-chain profile PDA is created
lazily by the order-bot on the first `/deposit/build-tx` or first `/mobile/orders`
placement that targets that `profileIndex`. `/mobile/balances` will return `usdc: 0` for
every uninitialized profile without erroring; that's a normal "this index has never been
used" response, not a provisioning gate.

`profileIndex` is required on every order, deposit, and balance call. Pick a convention
(e.g. profile 0 for default, 1+ for strategy buckets) and stick with it — there's no
server-side notion of a "primary" profile.

Each profile carries a **margin mode**: `isolated` (the default, and the only model on
every venue but Phoenix) or `unified` — see below. `GET
/passthrough/users/{wallet}/profiles` returns all six with their current mode.

## Cross margin (unified margin)

A profile set to `unified` routes its new positions onto Phoenix's **cross-margin seat**:
one collateral balance backing every market open on it, so a winning leg's equity supports
a losing one. Isolated profiles keep the per-position model — collateral belongs to the
order, and each position liquidates on its own.

Cross margin is Phoenix-only and per-profile. A common setup is profile 0 isolated for
multi-venue work and, say, profile 1 unified for a Phoenix portfolio.

### Turning it on

1. `PUT /passthrough/users/{wallet}/profiles/{index}/name` with `{"name": "..."}` — the
   margin mode lives on the row this creates, so an unnamed profile returns `400 "Name
   this profile before setting a margin mode"`.
2. `PUT /passthrough/users/{wallet}/profiles/{index}/margin-mode` with
   `{"marginMode": "unified"}` (or `"isolated"` to switch back).

Both accept either a JWT (`Authorization: Bearer`) or a Solana signature sent as `x-pubkey`
+ `x-signature` — over `imperial:profile-name:{wallet}:{index}` for the name call, and over
`imperial:margin-mode:{wallet}:{index}:{marginMode}` for the margin-mode call (the mode is
in the signed message, so a captured signature can't be replayed to flip it back). The
margin-mode response echoes the mode plus a `venueLock`
(`{"venues": ["phoenix"], "reason": "unified_margin"}` under unified). Apply that lock in
your own routing: it is a whitelist, and the api and order bot both reject a violating open
only after the round trip.

Switching is legal in either direction **with positions open** — there is no flat
requirement. That has a consequence worth building around: a live cross seat routinely
outlives a switch back to isolated, so an existing position's margin mode is a property of
the position, never of the profile's current flag. Read `directVenue.marginMode`
(`"cross"`) off the position row.

### What a unified profile may not do

These apply to **opens only** (`action: 0`). Closing, reducing, editing collateral, and
cancelling always work, on any venue the profile already holds a position on.

| Rejected | Why |
|----------|-----|
| Any `underwriter` other than `2` | The seat is Phoenix's. Switch to isolated to trade elsewhere. |
| Imperial Lending Pool loans | Loans are isolated-margin by construction; the program refuses every loan affordance on the cross seat. A profile holding an open loan also can't be switched to unified at all (`400`). |
| Markets with `isolatedOnly: true` on `GET /phoenix/markets` | Phoenix itself rejects them on the cross seat. |

### Sizing an open

On a cross seat `collateralAmount` is **not the position's margin** — it is a top-up
deposit into the seat, riding the same instruction as the increase. Per-leg leverage is not
a real quantity there; the seat as a whole margins every position.

Admission control is seat-wide. Let

- `free = effectiveCollateralUsd − initialMarginUsd` (both from
  `GET /phoenix/margin-account`), and
- `required = sizeUsd / maxLeverage` for the market (`maxLeverage` from
  `GET /phoenix/markets`, first tier).

The open is admitted when `free + collateralAmount ≥ required`. So `collateralAmount: 0` is
legal and normal once the seat has headroom — the leg opens against posted margin. The
check uses the market's headline leverage, so a position large enough to fall into a
lower-leverage tier needs more than `required`; Phoenix's own margin check is the final
authority and will still revert an oversized open.

### Reading seat state

`GET /phoenix/margin-account?walletAddress={wallet}&profileIndex={n}` returns the seat's
account-level figures, or `null` when the profile has never been onboarded onto one (a real
state, not an error — nothing has been deposited yet). This is the endpoint to poll before
the first trade, when there are no position rows to read figures off.

`GET /positions` carries the same object per profile as `phoenixCrossSeats[]` — in the same
response as the rows deliberately, so margin figures and positions are never from two
different instants. The `/ws` `position_state` frames carry rows **only**, so a cross-margin
bot still polls `/phoenix/margin-account` for margin and liquidation.

Every figure is a verbatim pass-through of Phoenix's own trader view — Imperial recomputes
no portfolio margin, and `riskState` / `riskTier` are Phoenix's words. An absent field means
Phoenix didn't report it: render it as unknown, never as `0`.

Key fields:

- `accountCollateralUsd` — deposited collateral. `effectiveCollateralUsd` — collateral plus
  discounted unrealised PnL, i.e. what actually backs positions.
- `initialMarginUsd` — what open positions and resting orders already consume. Free margin
  is the subtraction above.
- `maintenanceMarginUsd`, `riskState`, `riskTier` — Phoenix's liquidation-side view.
- `maxPositions` / `openPositions` — the seat's hard, unraisable ceiling on concurrent
  markets, and how many it currently holds. Phoenix has no resize instruction, so treat the
  ceiling as fixed.
- `liquidationPricesBySymbol` — per-market liquidation prices **as Phoenix computes them**,
  keyed by Phoenix's RAW symbol (`GOLD`, not `XAU`). A **`null` value** means Phoenix quotes
  no price for that market — routine on a cross seat, where a leg the rest of the balance
  absorbs long before maintenance is breached has no level of its own. The key stays present
  so the map still enumerates every market. Phoenix signals this with a negative price
  (`-1`); render `null` as unknown, never as `0` — a `$0` liquidation price on a long reads
  as "cannot be liquidated", which is the inverse of the truth here.

### Positions on a cross seat

- **Per-position liquidation fields are `null`**: `liquidationPrice`,
  `partialLiquidationPriceUsd`, and `breakevenPriceUsd` are suppressed on cross rows. They
  come from an isolated kernel that divides one position's collateral into one position's
  requirement, and on a shared seat neither term exists. Use
  `liquidationPricesBySymbol`. Note that a price there is the level at which *that market*
  becomes liable — Phoenix liquidates a cross seat by closing whichever positions its own
  engine picks, so it is not a promise about which leg dies.
- **`positionPda` is the trader account, shared by every leg on the seat.** Key your local
  state on `(positionPda, asset, side)`, not `positionPda` alone. Treat
  `/phoenix/margin-account` as authoritative for what the seat holds — `openPositions` and
  the keys of `liquidationPricesBySymbol` enumerate every market on it, including any leg
  the position rows haven't caught up with.
- `collateralUsd` and `leverageX` on the row still report what Imperial tracked as
  deposited against that leg. They are real numbers, but they are not the seat's margin —
  don't compute risk from them.

### Adding and removing margin

`POST /mobile/orders/collateral` with `underwriter: 2`, `action: 0` to add or `1` to
remove, and `marketMint` / `side` naming **any market currently open on the seat**. The
instruction is keyed on a market because every other venue holds collateral per position;
a cross seat has one balance, so the choice of market is transport, not scope.

The withdrawal cap is `effectiveCollateralForWithdrawalsUsd − initialMarginForWithdrawalsUsd`,
**not** free margin — Phoenix values a withdrawal on a stricter basis where unrealised
profit doesn't count out, and publishes both terms pre-derived. If it reports neither, do
not withdraw. The flat collateral fee is charged in both directions (it's a cash-movement
fee), so the seat receives `amount − fee` on an add and you receive `amount − fee` on a
remove.

## Trading bot quickstart

End-to-end flow for a bot that opens a position on one venue and hedges it on another.

1. **Auth** — `POST /mobile/connect` then `POST /mobile/exchange` to get a JWT (see
   "Authentication" above). All subsequent trading calls send `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`.
2. **Fund the profile** — `POST /deposit/build-tx` with `mode: "deposit"` returns a sponsored,
   partially-signed transaction that creates the profile (if new) and deposits USDC from the
   wallet's USDC ATA. Sign with the wallet's keypair and submit. Same endpoint with
   `mode: "withdraw"` pulls USDC back to the wallet. Skip if the profile is already funded
   for the size you want to trade. **Size deposits from `/route`'s `requiredDeposit`** (pass
   `wallet` for your exact fee tier), NOT from `expectedCostUsd`/`costBreakdown` — the
   breakdown's `borrow`/`expectedLiqCost` terms are hold-period expectations that are never
   reserved upfront, and sizing off them over-funds by an order of magnitude.
3. **Pick a venue pair** — `GET /funding-rates` returns one row per canonical symbol with
   per-venue funding/borrow rates. Decide which venue to long and which to short. For a
   single-venue trade, `GET /route?asset=...&side=...&notional=...` returns a cost-optimized
   recommendation.
4. **Check available USDC** — `GET /mobile/balances` returns the per-subaccount USDC balance
   in 6-decimal native units. Size each leg against this; an underfunded profile fails the
   margin check on submission.
5. **Open the legs** — `POST /mobile/orders` with `action=0` (Increase). Use `symbol` (e.g.
   `"SOL"`, `"XAU"`) plus `underwriter` to address the market — the same canonical symbol
   you read from `/funding-rates`. The server resolves it to the right `marketMint` per
   venue, including Phoenix synthetics that have no SPL mint of their own. Existing
   integrations can still send `marketMint` directly. Fire the legs sequentially: if the
   second leg fails, immediately submit a Decrease for the first to unwind. The endpoint
   returns HTTP 200 even on rejection — always inspect `success` and `error` (see
   "Trading-endpoint response convention" below). Successful resting orders return
   `orderPda`, which you can pass straight to `/mobile/orders/cancel` or `/update` without
   waiting for indexer catch-up. Phoenix orders auto-activate the trader account on first
   use; you don't need to call `/phoenix/register` first. Per-venue market lists are still
   available at `/phoenix/markets`, `/gmtrade/markets` if you need
   underlying details (orderbook PDAs, leverage tiers, fee tables).
6. **Track state** — subscribe to both WS endpoints. `/ws/market` pushes funding-rate / mark-
   price / depth updates so you don't have to poll (use the `venue: "index"` mark-price
   entries for the number Imperial marks with). `/ws` (with `subscribe` keyed on your
   wallet) pings you when your positions or orders change; opt into `positionState` for
   pushed rows instead of refetching `/positions`, and `tradeEvents` for the settled
   `/trades` row at close instead of re-polling `/trades`. There is no replay buffer on
   either socket — refetch on reconnect.
7. **Close the legs** — `POST /mobile/orders` with `action=1` (Decrease) on each leg. Use
   `closeBps` to size the close as a fraction of the live position: `10000` for a full
   close, `2500` for a quarter. A full close may equivalently send `sizeUsd = 0` with
   `closeBps` omitted. Avoid sizing closes by echoing the open's `sizeUsd`: venues that
   denominate positions in the target asset convert `sizeUsd` at the CURRENT
   oracle price, so any adverse price drift turns an intended full close into a partial
   that leaves a dust position behind — which the venue then rejects (`MinCollateral`).
   `closeBps` is evaluated against on-chain size at execution and is immune to that drift.
8. **Reclaim residue** — after closing a position whose collateral was non-USDC (long
   SOL/BTC/ETH custody on Jupiter leaves WSOL/WBTC/WETH on the profile), call
   `POST /passthrough/users/{wallet}/profiles/{index}/sync` to swap residue back to USDC
   and route to the user wallet. Idempotent. Pure-USDC venues (Phoenix shorts, USDC-margin
   profiles) don't need this step.

## Trading-endpoint response convention

`POST /mobile/orders[/batch|/cancel|/collateral|/update]` always returns HTTP 200 once the
request was well-formed and the order bot was reachable, even if the order was rejected
on-chain. Inspect the response body:

- `success: true` — order accepted, `signature` is the Solana tx signature.
- `success: false` — order rejected; `error` is a human-readable message and the raw bot
  error is logged server-side. Common cases: leverage too high, market closed, slippage
  exceeded, no matching open position for a close-side order.
- `errorCode` — machine-matchable code for programmatic branching, present on every valid
  submission rejection. Named codes: `LeverageTooHigh`, `LeverageTooLow`, `SlippageExceeded`,
  `MarketClosed`, `TradingPaused`, `PositionAlreadyClosed`, `MinCollateral`
  (open/increase collateral below the venue minimum), `ReduceBelowMinCollateral`
  (a partial close would leave dust below the venue minimum — close fully or reduce
  less), `InsufficientBalance`, `InsufficientVenueBalance`, `InsufficientMargin`,
  `SwapRouteUnavailable`, `PostOnlyWouldCross`, `ProfileHasOpenPositions`,
  `CancelViaAppOnly`, `LoanMarketNotWhitelisted`, `LoanVenueUnsupported`,
  `LoanSizeAddBreaksFloor`, `VenueCapacity` (the venue's pool/custody is at its cap),
  `VenuePriceFeedStale` (the venue's own mark-price feed failed its staleness/validity
  check and the venue refused to price the order — upstream of Imperial, nothing was
  submitted and no fee was charged; retry once the venue recovers), `VenueRejected`. The venue programs' Anchor 6000-range error numbers do not agree with
  each other, so they are
  resolved against the order's `underwriter`; a code in that band on a venue whose program
  gives it no user-actionable meaning reports `VenueRejected` rather than naming the wrong
  control. Any other on-chain rejection surfaces its raw program
  error as `Custom<N>` (e.g. `Custom6034`). Failures without a recognizable provider/program
  code use `UnknownTradeFailure` or `InternalError` rather than returning a null code.

HTTP 4xx is reserved for malformed input or auth failures (missing/invalid JWT, mismatched
wallet claim). HTTP 5xx is reserved for the server itself failing (database or order-bot
transport failures that aren't fully recoverable).

get.description:
# Read off the chain, not off a quote snapshot

`order_quote_snapshots` exists because on Jupiter and Phoenix the quoted
price is computed in the browser and is lost unless it is stashed. Armada
has no such problem — `imperial_sunrise` needs `expected_price` on chain to
bound its own price checks, and ACCEPT lands the fill beside it — so this
reads `sunrise_requests`, where both halves already sit on one row and both
came from the chain.

# What each number answers

- `medianBps` / `adverseBps`: **did the user get the price the order
  stated.** Positive is better for the user. ⚠ The reference is a
  CLIENT-supplied `market_price`, so this is not a statement about
  Imperial's spread.
- The counts and `rejects`: **of the requests that reached the chain, how
  many filled and why the rest did not.** Every reject carries the
  price-blind reason that refused it, which is what makes "we never reject
  on price direction" checkable rather than asserted.

get.description:
# This reads existing state — it opens nothing

The api already streams `order_book/{market}` and `market_stats/{market}`
for every Armada market, because a size-dependent quote cannot be built
from the touch. This endpoint is a projection of that in-memory feed, so a
browser polling it costs one map lookup and never a request to the venue.

# The freshness rule is the quote's, not a new one

A book is served under `SUNRISE_QUOTE_MAX_AGE_MS` — the CARRY bound, the
same one a quote is struck under. That is deliberately generous, because
`bookAgeMs` measures time since the book last **changed** and a quiet market
stops changing without the venue going anywhere. `venueReachable` is the
liveness signal, and it is a separate field for exactly that reason.

# The risk gate is not consulted

A halted or reduce-only market is still a market the user is looking at.
Hiding the venue's book because Imperial will not take more risk on it would
tell the user nothing true about the market.

Optional comma-separated list of venues the caller wants excluded
(e.g. `excludedVenues=phoenix,gmtrade`). When omitted, the handler
falls back to `profile_names.excluded_venues` via `wallet` +
`profile_index` if those are present. Sticky venues with open
positions still route there even if excluded — open positions take
precedence over exclusions.
parameters.name: excludedVenues

200.description: Best venue for the trade plus a per-venue cost breakdown. `costBreakdown.expectedLiqCost = pLiq × LossGivenLiq(venue)`, where `pLiq` is the Brownian first-passage probability that the position hits its liquidation barrier within the requested `holdHours` window (default 24h): `pLiq = 2 × Φ(−d / σ_period)` with `d = 1/leverage − mmr` and `σ_period = dailyVol × √(holdHours / 24)`. Pass `holdHours` if your strategy holds positions for materially longer or shorter than a day. `costBreakdown` is an expected round-trip cost model, NOT a funding requirement — its `borrow`/`expectedLiqCost` terms are lifecycle estimates that are never reserved upfront. Size deposits from `requiredDeposit` (top-level for the winner at the effective leverage, per-candidate at each venue's openable leverage); pass `wallet` so the deposit skim reflects your fee tier. `maxLeverage` is a size-independent per-market cap — do not scale it by notional. `desiredLeverage` is OPTIONAL (defaults to 1x, un-clamped): omit it to just read caps, supply it for accurate `clamped`/`recommendedVenue`/`requiredDeposit` at your target.

get.description:
A ranked, ready-to-trade grid — both directions at ±1/2/3/5/8% from live
spot, on both sides, cheapest ask (highest payout multiple) first, top 12.
Barriers the pool won't quote are omitted: a clamped ask, a barrier the
live cohort has already swept, a halted or stale market.

This is the shortcut past the pricing model. Take a row, pick a payout,
and submit — no need to reimplement `imperial_core::touch` to get a price.
Cached ~60s and quoted against a moving spot, so treat `askBps` as
indicative and let the premium budget absorb the drift.

get.description:
Every live one-touch binary market with its spot, on-chain pricing config,
live volatility state, and standing book inventory — everything needed to
price a barrier offline. Tenors are separate markets: group by underlying
(the symbol prefix before `TOUCH`) and pick by `config.cohortWindowSecs`.

Returns `[]` when the pairs subsystem is disabled. When touch trading is
paused every row comes back `halted: true` rather than disappearing, so a
client can keep rendering the market read-only.

Open contracts first, then finished ones newest-first, capped at 200. This
is the only view of touch positions — they do not appear on `/positions`,
`/trades`, or the `/ws` `position_state` stream, all of which are perp-only.
There is no push channel for touch yet; poll this endpoint.
